111	import AppKit
112	
113	/// The output level meter in the timeline bar (road map 2, phase 5b): the one
114	/// view of `LevelMeter.shared` — and, since road map 3's recorder panel, of
115	/// any other `LevelMeter` handed to `init(meter:)`. The default is `.shared`,
116	/// so `TimelineBar`'s `LevelMeterView()` and every chrome render are byte for
117	/// byte what they were; the panel binds one to `ScreenRecorder.shared.meter`,
118	/// because a microphone published to `.shared` would light the timeline bar's
119	/// meter with the microphone (`ScreenRecorder`'s doc).
120	///
121	/// **The measurement is the model's, the ballistics are the view's.** What
122	/// arrives is a `LevelMeterReading` — per channel peak and RMS as linear
123	/// magnitude, already multiplied by the plan's envelope. Peak hold, the fall
124	/// and the clip dwell are display behaviour and live here, which is what lets
125	/// the phase's proof assert on the number without photographing a window.
126	/// `LevelMeter.swift`'s header argues the rest, including why the meter reads
127	/// the DSP tap that already exists instead of the second PostEffects tap the
128	/// road map asked for (there is one `audioTapProcessor` per input parameters
129	/// object, so that tap cannot be built).
130	///
131	/// **It subscribes itself, so nothing in the frozen files changes.** The model
132	/// is process-wide and `addObserver` hands back a token whose lifetime is the
133	/// subscription, so this view needs no handle kept for it in `TimelineView`,
134	/// no fan-out line in `EditorViewController` and no `setLevels` to call —
135	/// phase 5b touches neither frozen file.
136	///
137	/// **Where it sits, and why it is not beside the tracks it sums.** The bar
138	/// spans the whole window — `timelineContainer` is the bottom arranged subview
139	/// of `mainSplit`, pinned root leading→trailing — so its right end is under
140	/// the 304 pt inspector column, nowhere near the lanes. That is deliberate and
141	/// is not a bug to fix by moving the meter over the tracks: the meter is the
142	/// MIX, not a track, and the homes that would put it nearer the audio all
143	/// reopen a settled decision (the window toolbar has one job; a track header
144	/// at S has no 12 pt to give and repaints the whole column when anything in it
145	/// changes; the inspector is per-clip; a status bar is refused outright by the
146	/// design handoff).
147	///
148	/// **It goes in the flexible gap immediately left of the zoom cluster, and it
149	/// carries no divider.** `TimelineBar.build` states that arithmetic where the
150	/// row is assembled. What it means here is that the meter must survive being
151	/// starved: it has hugging AND compression resistance at priority 1, a
152	/// `lessThanOrEqualTo` cap so it cannot become a progress bar on a wide
153	/// window, and a `guard bounds.width` that lets it VANISH rather than draw a
154	/// scale too small to read — `TimelineSelectionBlock.draw`'s own
155	/// `guard textWidth > 8` precedent. Measured: at the 900 pt minimum window the
156	/// whole chrome renders BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the build before this phase, and
157	/// at 1080 and 1440 the only pixels that change are the meter's own 120 × 12.
158	///
159	/// **One resting appearance, always drawn.** The offscreen chrome harness has
160	/// no player, so every chrome render photographs this view at rest, and the
161	/// harness writes a PNG only when two consecutive captures are byte-identical.
162	/// So there is no free-running animation: the 30 Hz tick starts only when a
163	/// non-silent reading arrives and INVALIDATES ITSELF once the model has gone
164	/// silent and every bar has fallen to the floor —
165	/// `TimelineView.flashRefusal`'s shape, the project's one idiom for a bounded
166	/// repeating tick. Offscreen the model is silent, so no timer ever starts and
167	/// the view is static from its first draw.
168	final class LevelMeterView: NSView {
169	    // MARK: - Metrics
170	
171	    /// The size the bar's stack view asks for. 120 pt reads a −60…0 dB scale
172	    /// at about 2 pt per dB; 12 pt is two 5 pt channel rows and the gap
173	    /// between them, well inside the 30 pt the other bar controls take.
174	    static let intrinsicWidth: CGFloat = 120
175	    static let intrinsicHeight: CGFloat = 12
176	    /// The cap on what the meter absorbs from the row's slack. Without it a
177	    /// wide window could hand the meter several hundred points, which reads as
178	    /// a progress bar rather than as a level. In practice the row's existing
179	    /// spacer wins the slack and the meter sits at its intrinsic width at
180	    /// every window size above the minimum; the cap is the guarantee, not the
181	    /// mechanism.
182	    static let maximumWidth: CGFloat = 160
183	    /// Below this the meter draws NOTHING rather than a scale nobody can read.
184	    private static let minimumWidth: CGFloat = 40
185	
186	    private static let channelGap: CGFloat = 2
187	    /// The clip cell at the right end of each channel row: always drawn, lit
188	    /// only on an over. Separating it from the scale is what keeps the resting
189	    /// state legible as a meter rather than as an empty pill.
190	    private static let clipCell: CGFloat = 3
191	    private static let clipGap: CGFloat = 2
192	
193	    // MARK: - Ballistics
194	
195	    /// The bottom of the SCALE — not `LevelMeterMath.floorDB`, which is −120
196	    /// and exists to keep a logarithm finite. Linear in dB from here to
197	    /// 0 dBFS: a mapping a reader can predict, at the cost of spending a third
198	    /// of the width on the quietest 20 dB.
199	    private static let scaleFloorDB: Float = -60
200	    /// Instant attack, 24 dB/s fall — near IEC's peak-programme fallback, fast
201	    /// enough to track a cut and slow enough to read at 30 Hz.
202	    private static let fallDBPerSecond: Float = 24
203	    /// The hold mark dwells, then falls at half the bar's rate.
204	    private static let holdFallDBPerSecond: Float = 12
205	    private static let holdSeconds: TimeInterval = 1.2
206	    /// How long an over stays lit — long enough to catch out of the corner of
207	    /// an eye while playback runs on.
208	    private static let clipSeconds: TimeInterval = 2
209	    private static let tickInterval: TimeInterval = 1.0 / 30
210	
211	    /// One channel's animated state, all three levels in dBFS.
212	    private struct Bar {
213	        var rms: Float
214	        var peak: Float
215	        var hold: Float
216	        var holdUntil: Date
217	        var clipUntil: Date
218	
219	        static let rest = Bar(
220	            rms: LevelMeterView.scaleFloorDB, peak: LevelMeterView.scaleFloorDB,
221	            hold: LevelMeterView.scaleFloorDB, holdUntil: .distantPast,
222	            clipUntil: .distantPast)
223	
224	        var isResting: Bool {
225	            hold <= LevelMeterView.scaleFloorDB && Date() >= clipUntil
226	        }
227	    }
228	
229	    /// Left then right, always both: `LevelMeterReading` is two channels by
230	    /// construction (a mono track is widened downstream of the tap and a 5.1
231	    /// one is reported by its first two), so the meter's SHAPE never changes
232	    /// and the resting appearance is simply both bars at the floor.
233	    private var bars: [Bar] = [.rest, .rest]
234	    private var lastTick = Date.distantPast
235	    private var tick: Timer?
236	    private var observation: LevelMeterObservation?
237	    /// The model this view draws — `.shared` unless the caller says otherwise.
238	    private let meter: LevelMeter
239	
240	    // MARK: - Life cycle
241	
242	    init(meter: LevelMeter = .shared) {
243	        self.meter = meter
244	        super.init(frame: .zero)
245	        translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
246	        setContentHuggingPriority(NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
247	        setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
248	            NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
249	        widthAnchor.constraint(lessThanOrEqualToConstant: Self.maximumWidth).isActive = true
250	        setAccessibilityRole(.levelIndicator)
251	        setAccessibilityLabel("Output levels")
252	        // Dropping the token unsubscribes, so the meter's whole teardown is
253	        // this view's own lifetime and nothing has to remember to detach it.
254	        observation = meter.addObserver { [weak self] reading in
255	            self?.wake(reading)
256	        }
257	    }
258	
259	    @available(*, unavailable)
260	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
261	        fatalError("LevelMeterView does not support NSCoder")
262	    }

274	    // MARK: - The tick
275	
276	    /// A published reading only ever STARTS the clock; the clock then POLLS
277	    /// the model.
278	    ///
279	    /// That asymmetry is deliberate. `LevelMeter.publish` notifies observers
280	    /// only when the reading CHANGES, and a steady tone measured over
281	    /// identical buffers publishes the same four floats every time — so a
282	    /// meter that decayed between callbacks would fall to silence over exactly
283	    /// the material a level proof is written against. Polling `reading` on the
284	    /// tick reads what is true now, and the model's own silence — which
285	    /// `Playback` publishes when the rate drops to zero and again from its
286	    /// `deinit` — is what releases the meter.
287	    private func wake(_ reading: LevelMeterReading) {
288	        guard tick == nil, !reading.isSilent else { return }
289	        lastTick = Date()
290	        tick = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: Self.tickInterval, repeats: true) {
291	            [weak self] timer in
292	            guard let self = self else {
293	                timer.invalidate()
294	                return
295	            }
296	            self.advance(timer)
297	        }
298	    }
299	
300	    /// One step of the ballistics, then one redraw.
301	    ///
302	    /// When the model has gone silent the bars fall to the floor and the timer
303	    /// invalidates itself, which is what leaves the meter — and the run loop —
304	    /// exactly as they were before playback started.
305	    private func advance(_ timer: Timer) {
306	        let now = Date()
307	        let elapsed = Float(min(max(now.timeIntervalSince(lastTick), 0), 0.5))
308	        lastTick = now
309	        let reading = meter.reading
310	        let releasing = reading.isSilent
311	        bars[0] = step(
312	            bars[0], peak: reading.peakLeft, rms: reading.rmsLeft,
313	            elapsed: elapsed, now: now, releasing: releasing)
314	        bars[1] = step(
315	            bars[1], peak: reading.peakRight, rms: reading.rmsRight,
316	            elapsed: elapsed, now: now, releasing: releasing)
317	        if releasing, bars.allSatisfy({ $0.isResting }) {
318	            timer.invalidate()
319	            tick = nil
320	            bars = [.rest, .rest]
321	        }
322	        needsDisplay = true
323	    }
324	
325	    /// Instant attack, timed fall, and a hold that dwells before it follows.
326	    /// `hold` is never below `peak` and `peak` is never below `rms`, so the
327	    /// three marks can only ever be drawn left to right.
328	    ///
329	    /// `releasing` is the silent case, and it drops the hold's dwell and falls
330	    /// it at the bar's own rate. Without that an over would leave its mark
331	    /// sinking for six seconds after playback stopped, which both reads wrong
332	    /// (the meter is no longer measuring anything) and keeps the tick alive
333	    /// for six seconds to say so. With it the whole tail is bounded by the
334	    /// clip cell's two seconds and a fall from the top of the scale: the meter
335	    /// is back at rest, and the timer gone, inside about 2.6 s.
336	    private func step(
337	        _ bar: Bar, peak: Float, rms: Float, elapsed: Float, now: Date, releasing: Bool
338	    ) -> Bar {
339	        var next = bar
340	        let fall = Self.fallDBPerSecond * elapsed
341	        next.rms = max(Self.scaled(rms), max(bar.rms - fall, Self.scaleFloorDB))
342	        next.peak = max(Self.scaled(peak), max(bar.peak - fall, Self.scaleFloorDB))
343	        next.rms = min(next.rms, next.peak)
344	        if !releasing, next.peak >= next.hold {
345	            next.hold = next.peak
346	            next.holdUntil = now.addingTimeInterval(Self.holdSeconds)
347	        } else if releasing || now >= next.holdUntil {
348	            let rate = releasing ? Self.fallDBPerSecond : Self.holdFallDBPerSecond
349	            next.hold = max(next.peak, max(next.hold - rate * elapsed, Self.scaleFloorDB))
350	        }
351	        if peak >= 1 {
352	            next.clipUntil = now.addingTimeInterval(Self.clipSeconds)
353	        }
354	        return next
355	    }
356	
357	    /// Linear magnitude to a level on THIS scale. The conversion itself is the
358	    /// model's — one implementation of dBFS in the phase, not two — and this
359	    /// only lifts its −120 floor to the bottom of the drawn scale.
360	    private static func scaled(_ magnitude: Float) -> Float {
361	        max(scaleFloorDB, LevelMeterMath.decibels(magnitude))
362	    }
363	
364	    // MARK: - Drawing
365	
366	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
367	        guard bounds.width >= Self.minimumWidth else { return }
368	        let scaleWidth = bounds.width - Self.clipCell - Self.clipGap
369	        guard scaleWidth > 0 else { return }
370	
371	        let now = Date()
372	        let rows = CGFloat(bars.count)
373	        let gaps = Self.channelGap * (rows - 1)
374	        let rowHeight = max(1, ((bounds.height - gaps) / rows).rounded(.down))
375	        let top = ((bounds.height - (rowHeight * rows + gaps)) / 2).rounded()
376	
377	        for (index, bar) in bars.enumerated() {
378	            let y = top + CGFloat(index) * (rowHeight + Self.channelGap)
379	
380	            let trough = NSRect(x: 0, y: y, width: scaleWidth, height: rowHeight)
381	            DS.meterTrough.setFill()
382	            trough.fill()
383	
384	            let cell = NSRect(
385	                x: bounds.width - Self.clipCell, y: y,
386	                width: Self.clipCell, height: rowHeight)
387	            (now < bar.clipUntil ? DS.meterClip : DS.meterTrough).setFill()
388	            cell.fill()
389	
390	            // The instantaneous peak washes the trough behind the RMS bar, so
391	            // one glance gives both the body of the sound and its transients.
392	            let peakWidth = Self.width(forDB: bar.peak, in: scaleWidth)
393	            if peakWidth > 0 {
394	                DS.meterFill.withAlphaComponent(0.35).setFill()
395	                NSRect(x: 0, y: y, width: peakWidth, height: rowHeight).fill()
396	            }
397	            let rmsWidth = Self.width(forDB: bar.rms, in: scaleWidth)
398	            if rmsWidth > 0 {
399	                DS.meterFill.setFill()
400	                NSRect(x: 0, y: y, width: rmsWidth, height: rowHeight).fill()
401	            }
402	            // The hold mark. It is never behind the RMS bar (`step` keeps the
403	            // three ordered), so it always reads against the trough or against
404	            // the wash and needs no fourth ink of its own.
405	            let holdWidth = Self.width(forDB: bar.hold, in: scaleWidth)
406	            if holdWidth > 0 {
407	                DS.meterFill.setFill()
408	                NSRect(
409	                    x: min(holdWidth, scaleWidth) - 2, y: y, width: 2, height: rowHeight
410	                ).fill()
411	            }
412	        }
413	    }
414	
415	    /// A level in dBFS to a width on the scale, linear in dB from the floor to
416	    /// 0 dBFS. Anything above 0 pins at full — saying an over is the clip
417	    /// cell's job, not the bar's.
418	    private static func width(forDB decibels: Float, in scale: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
419	        let fraction = (min(decibels, 0) - scaleFloorDB) / -scaleFloorDB
420	        guard fraction > 0 else { return 0 }
421	        return (CGFloat(min(fraction, 1)) * scale).rounded()
422	    }
423	}

611	/// momentary and short-term bars, and the Normalize target as a 1 pt accent
612	/// line (read at draw; the panel redraws it on a defaults change, so a target
613	/// changed while paused shows at once).
614	final class LoudnessScaleView: NSView {
615	    static let floorLUFS = -48.0
616	    var momentary: Double? { didSet { if momentary != oldValue { needsDisplay = true } } }
617	    var shortTerm: Double? { didSet { if shortTerm != oldValue { needsDisplay = true } } }

624	    /// The height a level sits at in a plot `height` tall.
625	    static func y(_ lufs: Double, in plot: NSRect) -> CGFloat {
626	        let clamped = min(0, max(floorLUFS, lufs))

636	            .font: DS.mono(9), .foregroundColor: DS.textFaint,

648	        }

650	            let column = NSRect(

652	                width: Self.barWidth, height: plot.height)

158	            // nest carrying anything audible has audio properties of its own,

162	            // `AudioPane.normalizable`, which is what keeps a greyed button
163	            // and a live menu item from disagreeing about one selection.
164	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }

168	            // button asks it through `AudioPane.normalizable`.
169	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }
170	            return selectedClips.contains { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }
171	        case #selector(matchAudio(_:)):
172	            // Two clips Normalize could measure (AU-121): one the reference.
173	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }
174	            return selectedClips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }.count >= 2

177	            // reason above; `read` and `plan` may still refuse, by name.

content.content:
## The level meter

The level meter is in the timeline bar, just left of the zoom controls. While the timeline plays, it shows the mix you are hearing:

- **Two rows**, one per channel, on a −60 to 0 dB scale.
- **A solid bar** for the average (RMS) level, with a lighter wash behind it showing the instantaneous peak.
- **A peak-hold mark** that stays at the highest recent level for about 1.2 seconds and then falls.
- **A clip cell** at the right end of each row. It lights for 2 seconds whenever a sample reaches full scale.

The meter includes everything that shapes what you hear: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, and the compressor and other effects. At normal speed it shows the mix itself, so two tracks playing the same sound read as one louder sound, and a sound and its inverse read as silence. At other speeds it adds up each track's level, which can read a little higher than the mix. When playback stops, the bars fall back to the floor. If two projects are open, the meter follows the one that is playing. On a very narrow window there isn't room for the meter, so it is hidden.

The screen recorder panel has its own meter for the microphone. See [Screen recording](screen-recording.md).

## Live loudness

Choose **View ▸ Loudness Meter** (⌃⌘L) to show a column at the right of the preview, left of the scopes. While the preview plays at normal speed, it measures the mix you hear, the way loudness standards (EBU R 128, ITU-R BS.1770) do:

- **Two bars**, M and S, on a −48 to 0 LUFS scale. A thin line marks the Normalize target (−16 LUFS unless you changed it).
- **Momentary**: the last 0.4 seconds.
- **Short-term**: the last 3 seconds.
- **Integrated**: everything measured since the last reset, with quiet passages left out as the standard says.
- **True peak max**: the highest true peak since the last reset. It turns coral above −1 dBTP.

Click the **Reset** button at the top of the column to start measuring again. The meter also starts again on its own when you jump to another place: a seek, the loop going round, or playing from somewhere else. Pausing and playing on doesn't reset it, and nor does an edit, a gap between clips or holding a menu open. When playback stops, the figures stay where they were.

The meter measures only at normal speed. At any other speed, Momentary and Short-term show "—" and the column says "Measured only at normal speed."; Integrated and True peak max keep their values. A dash means there isn't a figure yet; "−∞" means digital silence.

The figures are the mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness setting and its master limiter, and the column says so. While any track has a compressor or limiter, it says they are approximate (see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter)). An export with a loudness target changes the level after this point, and the master limiter holds its peaks under the ceiling, so its report can differ. The column is per window and turns off when you close the window.

*Agents:* there is no product tool; an agent reads loudness from an export's report or a clip's loudness read-out.

## Loudness on export

The level meter in the timeline bar shows peaks, not loudness; the Loudness Meter column shows the preview's loudness. To make an export hit a loudness target, such as integrated LUFS with a true-peak ceiling, use the export sheet's loudness option: the export reaches it through its master limiter, which holds every export's peaks under −1 dBTP. A WAV or AIFF can be written at 24 bits. Every export reports what its sound measured, whether or not you normalized it. See [Export](export.md).

An audio export can also write **stems**: each track's sound, or each track name's, as its own file beside the mix, for mixing or mastering in another editor. A stem is its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness target and no master limiter, so the stems add up to the mix. Choose them in the export sheet's **Stems** row. See [Stems](export.md#stems).

## Synchronize Audio

**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** lines up two or more clips by their sound. The usual case is a camera clip and a separate audio recorder that captured the same moment. Select the clips, each on its own track, and choose the command. One clip, the **anchor**, stays where it is. Every other clip slides along its own track until its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's.

The anchor is chosen this way:

1. Among the selected clips that have a picture, the one that starts earliest. If none of them has a picture, all of the clips are considered.
2. If two start at the same time, the one on the rearmost track.
3. If they are still tied, the one created first.

In other words, a camera clip stays put and the recorder moves to it.

### What it does

- **It matches the sound itself.** Each file's sound is analysed once when it's imported, so differences in gain, microphone and room don't stop a match. When both clips contain enough speech, at least 2 seconds as judged by the on-device voice model, only the speech is compared.
- **It searches the trimmed parts first.** Frame Job first looks for a match within the parts of each clip you have trimmed it to. It searches the whole files only if that finds nothing and one of the clips is trimmed. If a recording contains more than one similar stretch, trim the recorder roughly around the camera's sound so it matches the right one.
- **It checks the waveforms.** A match is used only if the two waveforms also line up there, as a clear peak within 48 ms. This keeps two takes of the same words from being treated as one recording. The check also fine-tunes the offset to less than a frame.
- **It corrects drift.** If two clocks run at slightly different rates, the recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift and corrects it by playing the clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1. The correction is a plain resample, so the pitch moves very slightly with it. Drift is left alone when it is under 5 ms over the overlap, when it is too small to tell from no drift (under three times its own uncertainty), or when the speed it needs is more than 0.2 % from ×1. The corrected speed appears in the clip's Speed section (for example ×1.0004), with Keep pitch turned off. The command shows no drift figure of its own; that speed is where the correction shows. Like any clip at a speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, the corrected clip's sound is rendered in the background, so it is briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change of it (see [Speed](speed.md)); an export waits for it.
- **It trims the head if needed.** If a clip would have to start before 0:00 to line up, it loses just that much from its start instead, and starts at 0:00 in sync. The anchor is never moved or trimmed.
- **Moves land on whole frames.** Clips move by a whole number of frames. A whole command is one undo step, named "Synchronize Audio".

### The Synchronizing Audio sheet

Matching runs in the background while a **Synchronizing Audio** sheet is shown. The sheet has a progress bar and the line "Matching the sound of N clips…". **Cancel** (Escape) closes it and leaves everything as it was. Nothing moves until a match is found. If you change the project while matching is still running, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.

### Confident and weak matches

A match is **confident** when its best candidate is clearly stronger than every other offset: a confidence of at least 10 and at least 1.5 above the next candidate. A confident match is applied straight away.

A match is **weak** when no candidate is confident, but the best one within about 3 seconds of where the clip already sits has a confidence of at least 4. Because a weak match might be unrelated sound, it is never applied without asking. A **Weak match** sheet appears, for example:

> Weak match: move “record.aifc” 0.80 s earlier (trimming 0.80 s off its head)?

A clip that doesn't need to move, only to have its drift corrected, is asked about this way instead:

> Weak match: play “record.aifc” at ×1.0004, correcting its drift?

When several clips are weak, one sheet lists them all, separated by semicolons.

Under the question, the sheet gives the anchor's name, each match's confidence and the rule the match fell short of. **Apply** (the default button) makes every listed change as one undo step. **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.

When nothing matches, the command is refused. The refusal names the offsets it did find and their confidences, so you can move the clip near the right one and try again.

### When it refuses

From the menu, clips in the selection that play no sound (a still, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off) and nests are left out without a message, and the command needs at least two other clips with sound. To synchronize clips inside a nest, open it (⌘↓) and select them there.

Synchronize Audio is all or nothing. If any clip can't be matched, nothing moves. Frame Job beeps and lists every reason at the foot of the inspector. A clip can't be synchronized when it:

- has no sound to line up by (its analysis found no sound at all)
- is still being analysed. Its sound features or speech haven't been written yet, so try again in a moment.
- holds under 2 seconds of sound
- plays more than 0.2 % away from ×1
- plays at a rate other than its speed setting
- plays reversed
- ramps its speed (a speed action changes its rate over its length)
- would share a track with another clip being synchronized
- would never play at the same time as the anchor once lined up
- matches the anchor's sound, but the waveforms don't line up there (for example two takes of the same words), so they are not one recording
- matches the anchor's sound, but the two share less than 2 seconds of waveform there, too little to confirm it is one recording
- would overlap another clip on its own track after the move
- would lose so much of its head that less than a frame is left

If the clips are already in sync, nothing changes and Frame Job beeps. The menu item is enabled only when at least two selected clips that aren't nests can play sound.

*Agents:* `sync_audio` (`clips`, at least two; optional `anchor`; optional `accept_weak`). A weak match answers `moved: false` and lists its clips under `weak`. Call again with `accept_weak: true` only after the person has agreed to that move. The answer reports each clip's offset, confidence, search, drift and trim. Unlike the menu, the tool refuses a nest or a clip that plays no sound by name.

## The level meter

The two-channel meter in the timeline bar shows the mix while the project
plays and drops to silence when it stops. In a narrow window it gets smaller
and can disappear. It's described on [Audio](audio.md).

## The preview

### Preview Quality

**View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** Full, Half or Quarter draws the preview at a
fraction of the canvas size and scales it back up to fit. It makes heavy
projects play more smoothly. It never changes an export, a saved frame or a
rendered frame. The menu checks the current choice, Full is the default, and
the choice is remembered. The Preview Window (below) shows the same player,
so it draws at the same quality.

### A second preview window

**View ▸ Preview Window** (⇧⌘P) opens the picture in its own window, titled
"<project> — Preview", with no handles or guides drawn over it. Use it to
put the picture on a second display; it can go full screen. It shows the same
player as the main preview, so the two never drift apart. The menu item has a
checkmark while the window is open, and the same key hides it again. The

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio and `sync_audio` (road maps "audio-sync", AS-1 and
4	/// AS-2, and "audio-sync-2", AS-3 and AS-4; spec §11 SY-1..SY-21): selected clips that
5	/// play sound are lined up by their sound. One ANCHOR stays where it is and every other clip moves by a
6	/// frame-snapped `move_clip`, its clock drift corrected by a `set_speed`, all
7	/// as one undo step — or the whole command refuses, naming every reason at
8	/// once (SY-1).
9	///
10	/// `AudioNormalize`'s shape: `read` takes everything off the document once
11	/// (the edited project's snapshot and plan, and each file's cached sync
12	/// features, samples and speech probabilities), and `plan` is pure — readings
13	/// in, ops or a refusal out. The menu item and the tool call the same pair,
14	/// so neither measures anything of its own. The signal arithmetic is
15	/// `AudioSyncMatch`'s, the sub-frame refinement `AudioSyncPHAT`'s (SY-20),
16	/// where to look and what to choose
17	/// `AudioSync+Search.swift`'s, and which planned moves are only WEAK — asked
18	/// about, never applied silently (SY-18, SY-19) — `AudioSync+Weak.swift`'s.
19	///
20	/// **Time.** A reading's `zero` is the project tick at which its file's
21	/// source tick 0 would play (`segment.start − round(segment.sourceIn /
22	/// speed)`), and its features are resampled onto its timeline grid (frame k
23	/// = source frame k·speed; themselves at ×1), and so are its speech masks
24	/// (SY-17, frame k = source frame round(k·speed)), so a sound at timeline
25	/// frame `f` plays at `zero + f·9600`; its samples are read at `t·speed`
26	/// where they are used (SY-20). A mover whose sound at frame `m` is the
27	/// anchor's at `m + lag` lines up when its zero becomes `zeroA + lag·9600`:
28	/// `delta = zeroA − zeroN + lag·9600`, snapped to the frame grid (SY-4),
29	/// because the model stores no sub-frame time.
30	///
31	/// **Drift and the refinement** (SY-6, SY-20, SY-21, SY-29). Over the overlap
32	/// the coarse delta gives, the lag is fitted as a line, `lag(a) = c + ρ·a` (a
33	/// an anchor timeline sample, 75 ticks each, c in samples); not measured, the
34	/// line is the coarse lag. PHAT along it over the 30 s of the overlap whose
35	/// features agree most (SY-32) — the files' overlap at the lag when that played
36	/// overlap is under 2 s — shifts c by a clear peak's sub-sample shift. **The
37	/// waveform gate** (SY-29): a match of either tier stands only on that clear
38	/// peak; a peak that is not clear refuses the command (`incoherent`), and so
39	/// does a refinement that cannot run (`unconfirmed`) unless neither reading
40	/// carries samples at all, when the features' tier stands. Corrected
41	/// (SY-8), the mover's speed becomes `s' = s·(1 − ρ)` and, since `set_speed`
42	/// keeps its start S and in point I, source tick μ plays at `S + δ + (μ −
43	/// I)/s'` — on the anchor's line everywhere when `δ = snapToFrame(round(zeroA
44	/// + 75·c/(1 − ρ) − S + I/s'))` (`correctedDelta`). Left uncorrected, it is
45	/// placed by the line's value at the overlap's centre aMid, `delta =
46	/// snapToFrame(zeroA − zeroN + round((c + ρ·aMid)·75))`; not measured, by
47	/// the (refined) lag. Snapping leaves one constant offset of at most half a
48	/// frame.
49	///
50	/// **The head trim** (SY-16, the owner's choice): a mover that would start
51	/// before 0 loses the excess off its head by a `trim_start` between the
52	/// `set_speed` and the `move_clip`, so it starts at 0 and what remains plays
53	/// in sync. **What it refuses rather than lets the core decide** (SY-4):
54	/// `move_clip` clamps the earliest clip at 0, and on an overlap within the
55	/// overlap rule it ADDS a cross dissolve instead of refusing — so a mover
56	/// that would land on another clip of its own track is refused here, by
57	/// name — on the FINAL span, after any change of speed or trim (SY-10).
58	enum AudioSync {
59	
60	    // MARK: - Vocabulary
61	
62	    /// One reason the command will not run: about a clip ("clip N: …") or
63	    /// about the selection as a whole (the reason alone).
64	    struct Problem: Equatable {
65	        let clip: UInt32?
66	        let reason: String
67	
68	        var description: String {
69	            guard let clip = clip else { return reason }
70	            return "clip \(clip): \(reason)"
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    /// Another top-level clip on a reading's track, as the span it occupies.
75	    struct Neighbour: Equatable {
76	        let clip: UInt32
77	        let start: Ticks
78	        let end: Ticks
79	    }
80	
81	    /// One clip that can be matched: where it sits, where its file's tick 0
82	    /// plays, whether it has pictures (the anchor rule, SY-2), its file's
83	    /// samples and sync features, and the clips it shares its track with.
84	    struct Reading: Equatable {
85	        let clip: UInt32
86	        let media: UInt32
87	        let trackIndex: Int
88	        let start: Ticks
89	        let end: Ticks
90	        let zero: Ticks
91	        let hasVideo: Bool
92	        /// Its file's 8 kHz samples (`cache/sync/<id>.pcm`) on the SOURCE grid.
93	        let samples: [Int16]
94	        /// Its file's `SyncFeatures` frames on the SOURCE grid, frame-major.
95	        let features: [Float]
96	        /// Which of those frames are speech (SY-17), one per frame on the
97	        /// SOURCE grid; nil when the voice model cannot be used.
98	        let speech: [Bool]?
99	        let neighbours: [Neighbour]
100	        /// The clip's playback rate, within SY-9's band.
101	        let speed: Double
102	        /// Its first audio segment's in point, in source ticks.
103	        let sourceIn: Ticks
104	    }
105	
106	    /// Everything a run reads, taken off the document once.
107	    struct Input {
108	        let readings: [Reading]
109	        let problems: [Problem]
110	        /// The anchor the caller named, or nil for SY-2's rule.
111	        let anchor: UInt32?
112	        let fps: Fps
113	    }
114	
115	    /// One mover's answer: its lag in ticks (refined, at the overlap's
116	    /// centre), the coarse lag and the refinement (SY-20), the frame-snapped
117	    /// move, where it lands, how sure the match was and how it was found,
118	    /// what drift it measured, its speed, duration and correction after the
119	    /// command, and the head it lost to start at 0 (SY-16).
120	    struct Synced: Equatable {
121	        let clip: UInt32
122	        let media: UInt32
123	        let lag: Ticks
124	        /// The coarse match's lag in ticks, before the refinement.
125	        let coarseLag: Ticks
126	        /// The PHAT refinement over the overlap; nil when none ran.
127	        let refinement: AudioSyncPHAT.Refinement?
128	        let delta: Ticks
129	        let start: Ticks
130	        /// The chosen lag's z-score (SY-12).
131	        let confidence: Double
132	        let search: Search
133	        let chosenBy: ChosenBy
134	        let matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn
135	        let candidates: [CandidateMove]
136	        let drift: AudioSyncMatch.DriftAnswer
137	        let speed: Double
138	        let duration: Ticks
139	        let correction: Correction
140	        let trimmed: Ticks
141	    }
142	
143	    enum Plan {
144	        case refused([Problem])
145	        case planned(anchor: UInt32, synced: [Synced], ops: [ReelOp])
146	    }
147	
148	    // MARK: - Offering it
149	
150	    /// Whether the command can be offered: at least two selected clips pass
151	    /// `AudioNormalize.canOffer` (sound, and not a nest). A cheap pre-check
152	    /// of the snapshot, never the plan — `read` may still refuse.
153	    static func canOffer(_ clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
154	        clips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }.count >= 2
155	    }
156	
157	    // MARK: - Reading
158	
159	    /// Reads the edited project's snapshot, plan, sync features and samples
160	    /// and (with the voice model) speech probabilities for `clips` (nil:
161	    /// the document's selection). nil only when the plan cannot be read; a
162	    /// clip that cannot be matched is a `Problem`.
163	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]?, anchor: UInt32?)
164	        -> Input? {
165	        guard let plan = document.editedProject.plan else { return nil }
166	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
167	
168	        var audio: [UInt32: [PlanSegment]] = [:]
169	        for track in plan.audioTracks {
170	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
171	                audio[segment.clip, default: []].append(segment)
172	            }
173	        }
174	        var pictured: Set<UInt32> = []
175	        for track in plan.videoTracks {
176	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
177	                pictured.insert(segment.clip)
178	            }
179	        }
180	
181	        var samplesByMedia: [UInt32: [Int16]] = [:]
182	        var featuresByMedia: [UInt32: [Float]] = [:]
183	        var speechByMedia: [UInt32: [Float]] = [:]
184	        let voice = SileroVAD.isAvailable
185	        var readings: [Reading] = []
186	        var problems: [Problem] = []
187	        var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
188	        for id in clips ?? document.selection.sorted() where seen.insert(id).inserted {
189	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else {
190	                problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: "is not a clip in this project."))
191	                continue
192	            }
193	            if case .nest = clip.source {
194	                problems.append(
195	                    Problem(
196	                        clip: id,
197	                        reason: "is a nest, and a nest has no sound of its own to match: the "
198	                            + "waveform cache is per media file and the clips inside a nest "
199	                            + "each have their own. Open it (⌘↓) and synchronize the clips "
200	                            + "inside."))
201	                continue
202	            }
203	            // A ramp's rate changes over the clip, and the drift line reads
204	            // one (spec §11 SR-20 (e)); the map is the snapshot's handle's.
205	            if document.editedProject.sourceMap(id)?.ramped == true {
206	                problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: AudioSync.ramped))
207	                continue
208	            }
209	            guard let segments = audio[id]?.sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }),
210	                  let first = segments.first
211	            else {
212	                problems.append(
213	                    Problem(
214	                        clip: id,
215	                        reason: "plays no sound in this timeline, so there is nothing to line "
216	                            + "it up by. A still, a clip whose media has no audio track and a "
217	                            + "clip with audio switched off all read this way."))
218	                continue
219	            }
220	            if clip.speed != 1 || segments.contains(where: { $0.isTimeScaled }) {
221	                let scaled = segments.first { $0.isTimeScaled } ?? first
222	                let rate = clip.speed != 1
223	                    ? clip.speed : Double(scaled.sourceDuration) / Double(max(scaled.duration, 1))
224	                // At speed 1 a time-scaled segment is a stretch the clip's
225	                // speed does not say, so neither `zero` nor `set_speed` can
226	                // read it: refused, as AS-1 did (SY-9).
227	                if let problem = rateProblem(rate) ?? (clip.speed == 1 ? stretched(rate) : nil) {
228	                    problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: problem))
229	                    continue
230	                }
231	            }
232	            if case .media(_, _, true) = clip.source {
233	                problems.append(
234	                    Problem(
235	                        clip: id,
236	                        reason: "plays reversed; Synchronize Audio lines up clips playing "
237	                            + "forwards."))
238	                continue
239	            }
240	            let cached = featuresByMedia[first.media] ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
241	                MediaImporter.loadSyncFeatures(for: first.media, in: $0)
242	            }
243	            let probabilities = !voice ? nil : speechByMedia[first.media]
244	                ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
245	                    MediaImporter.loadSpeech(for: first.media, in: $0)
246	                }
247	            let pcm = samplesByMedia[first.media] ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
248	                MediaImporter.loadSyncSamples(for: first.media, in: $0)
249	            }
250	            // The samples are the features' own: a count that disagrees is a
251	            // pass not finished, read as not written.
252	            let written = cached.flatMap { features in
253	                pcm.flatMap {
254	                    SyncFeatures.frameCount(samples: $0.count)
255	                        == features.count / SyncFeatures.coefficients ? $0 : nil
256	                }
257	            }
258	            guard let features = cached, let samples = written, !voice || probabilities != nil
259	            else {
260	                // The waveform can be on the timeline while the features
261	                // and speech that land after it are not: say which.
262	                let missing = written == nil
263	                    ? " for Synchronize Audio — its sound features have not been written yet."
264	                    : " for Synchronize Audio — its speech has not been detected yet."
265	                problems.append(
266	                    Problem(
267	                        clip: id,
268	                        reason: "is still being analysed" + missing + " Try again in a moment."))
269	                continue
270	            }
271	            featuresByMedia[first.media] = features
272	            samplesByMedia[first.media] = samples
273	            if let probabilities { speechByMedia[first.media] = probabilities }
274	            let frames = features.count / SyncFeatures.coefficients
275	            guard frames >= AudioSyncMatch.minimumStretchFrames else {
276	                let seconds = String(
277	                    format: "%g",
278	                    Double(Ticks(AudioSyncMatch.minimumStretchFrames) * SyncFeatures.frameTicks)
279	                        / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
280	                problems.append(
281	                    Problem(
282	                        clip: id,
283	                        reason: "is too short to match: its file holds under \(seconds) s of "
284	                            + "sound."))
285	                continue
286	            }
287	            let neighbours = snapshot.clips
288	                .filter { $0.track == clip.track && $0.id != id }
289	                .map { Neighbour(clip: $0.id, start: $0.start, end: $0.start + $0.duration) }
290	            readings.append(
291	                Reading(
292	                    clip: id, media: first.media,
293	                    trackIndex: snapshot.tracks.firstIndex { $0.id == clip.track } ?? 0,
294	                    start: clip.start, end: clip.start + clip.duration,
295	                    zero: first.start - Ticks((Double(first.sourceIn) / clip.speed).rounded()),
296	                    hasVideo: pictured.contains(id), samples: samples, features: features,
297	                    speech: probabilities.map { AudioSyncMatch.speechMask($0, frames: frames) },
298	                    neighbours: neighbours,
299	                    speed: clip.speed, sourceIn: first.sourceIn))
300	        }
301	        return Input(
302	            readings: readings, problems: problems, anchor: anchor, fps: snapshot.canvas.fps)
303	    }
304	
305	    // MARK: - The anchor (SY-2)
306	
307	    /// The named reading; else, among the readings with pictures (all of them
308	    /// when none has), the earliest start, then the rearmost track, then the
309	    /// lowest id.
310	    static func chooseAnchor(_ readings: [Reading], named: UInt32?) -> Reading? {
311	        if let named = named { return readings.first { $0.clip == named } }
312	        let pictured = readings.filter { $0.hasVideo }
313	        let pool = pictured.isEmpty ? readings : pictured
314	        return pool.min { a, b in
315	            if a.start != b.start { return a.start < b.start }
316	            if a.trackIndex != b.trackIndex { return a.trackIndex < b.trackIndex }
317	            return a.clip < b.clip
318	        }
319	    }
320	
321	    // MARK: - Planning (SY-1, SY-4, SY-6..SY-10, SY-12..SY-16)
322	
323	    /// The ops, or every reason there are none. All or nothing: one problem
324	    /// anywhere refuses the whole command.
325	    static func plan(_ input: Input) -> Plan {
326	        guard input.problems.isEmpty else { return .refused(input.problems) }
327	        let readings = input.readings
328	        guard readings.count >= 2 else {
329	            return .refused([
330	                Problem(clip: nil, reason: "Synchronize Audio needs at least two clips with sound.")
331	            ])
332	        }
333	        guard let anchor = chooseAnchor(readings, named: input.anchor) else {
334	            return .refused([
335	                Problem(
336	                    clip: input.anchor,
337	                    reason: "is not one of the clips being synchronized, so it cannot be the "
338	                        + "anchor.")
339	            ])
340	        }
341	
342	        var problems: [Problem] = []
343	        var byTrack: [Int: [UInt32]] = [:]
344	        for reading in readings { byTrack[reading.trackIndex, default: []].append(reading.clip) }
345	        for index in byTrack.keys.sorted() {
346	            guard let ids = byTrack[index], ids.count > 1 else { continue }
347	            let names = ids.map { "clip \($0)" }.joined(separator: " and ")
348	            problems.append(
349	                Problem(
350	                    clip: nil,
351	                    reason: "\(names) are on one track; Synchronize Audio lines up clips on "
352	                        + "different tracks."))
353	        }
354	
355	        // A file with no sound cannot be matched; the problem is the silent
356	        // clip's own, so a silent anchor is named once, not on every mover.
357	        let silent = "has no sound to line up by."
358	        let anchorSilent = AudioSyncMatch.isSilent(anchor.features)
359	        if anchorSilent { problems.append(Problem(clip: anchor.clip, reason: silent)) }
360	        let anchorFrames = AudioSyncMatch.resampledFrames(anchor.features, speed: anchor.speed)
361	        let anchorSpeech = anchor.speech.map {
362	            AudioSyncMatch.resampledMask($0, speed: anchor.speed)
363	        }
364	
365	        let hop = Double(SyncFeatures.hop)
366	        let sample = Double(AudioSyncPHAT.sampleTicks)
367	        // SY-22: one setup for every refinement this plan makes.
368	        let fft = AudioSyncPHAT.FFT(log2n: AudioSyncPHAT.planLog2n)
369	        var synced: [Synced] = []
370	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []

372	            guard !AudioSyncMatch.isSilent(mover.features) else {

374	                continue
375	            }
376	            if anchorSilent { continue }
377	            let moverFrames = AudioSyncMatch.resampledFrames(mover.features, speed: mover.speed)

379	                AudioSyncMatch.resampledMask($0, speed: mover.speed)
380	            }

388	                continue

391	            }

396	            let window = max(0, lower)..<max(0, lower, upper)
397	            var drift = AudioSyncMatch.drift(
398	                anchor: anchorFrames, mover: moverFrames, anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech,
399	                moverSpeech: moverSpeech, anchorSamples: anchor.samples,
400	                moverSamples: mover.samples, anchorSpeed: anchor.speed, moverSpeed: mover.speed,
401	                lag: found.lag, overlap: window, fft: fft)

403	            // 2 s played, over the files' overlap at the lag instead (SY-29).

405	            if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
406	                line = AudioSyncPHAT.Line(intercept: fit.intercept, rate: fit.rate)
407	            }
408	            let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
409	            let played = refinementRegion(
410	                overlap: window, anchorFrames: anchorFrames, moverFrames: moverFrames,
411	                anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech, moverSpeech: moverSpeech, matchedOn: found.matchedOn,
412	                line: line)
413	            let reach = played.count >= AudioSyncPHAT.minimumRegionSamples
414	                ? played
415	                : refinementRegion(
416	                    overlap: filesOverlap(
417	                        lag: found.lag, anchorFrames: anchorFrames.count / width,
418	                        moverFrames: moverFrames.count / width),
419	                    anchorFrames: anchorFrames, moverFrames: moverFrames,
420	                    anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech, moverSpeech: moverSpeech,
421	                    matchedOn: found.matchedOn, line: line)
422	            let refinement = AudioSyncPHAT.refine(
423	                anchor: anchor.samples, anchorSpeed: anchor.speed, mover: mover.samples,
424	                moverSpeed: mover.speed, line: line, region: reach, fft: fft)

426	            // peak; a refinement that could not run refuses too, unless
427	            // neither reading carries samples at all.
428	            if let refinement, !refinement.clear {
429	                problems.append(
430	                    Problem(
431	                        clip: nil,
432	                        reason: incoherent(
433	                            anchor: anchor.clip, mover: mover.clip, delta: coarse,

457	                    refinedTicks = Ticks(((found.lag * hop + refinement.shift) * sample).rounded())
458	                    delta = ReelTime.snapToFrame(
459	                        anchor.zero - mover.zero + refinedTicks, fps: input.fps)
460	                }
461	            }
462	            let correction = Self.correction(for: drift, speed: mover.speed)
463	            var newSpeed: Double?
464	            if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
465	                let centre = Double(window.lowerBound + window.upperBound) / 2 * hop
466	                let line = Ticks(((fit.intercept + fit.rate * centre) * sample).rounded())
467	                refinedTicks = line
468	                delta = ReelTime.snapToFrame(anchor.zero - mover.zero + line, fps: input.fps)
469	                if case .apply(let speed) = correction {
470	                    newSpeed = speed
471	                    delta = correctedDelta(
472	                        anchor: anchor, mover: mover, drift: fit, speed: speed, fps: input.fps)
473	                }
474	            }
475	            let duration = mover.end - mover.start
476	            let newDuration = newSpeed.map {
477	                durationAtSpeed(duration, from: mover.speed, to: $0, fps: input.fps)
478	            } ?? duration
479	            // SY-16: what would fall before 0 is trimmed off the mover's head.
480	            let excess = max(0, -(mover.start + delta))
481	            let start = mover.start + delta + excess
482	            let end = mover.start + delta + newDuration
483	            guard newDuration - excess >= input.fps.frameDuration else {
484	                let seconds = Double(excess) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond)
485	                problems.append(
486	                    Problem(
487	                        clip: mover.clip,
488	                        reason: "would have to lose " + String(format: "%.2f", seconds)
489	                            + " s of its head to start at 0, leaving under a frame of it."))
490	                continue
491	            }
492	            // Corrected and growing, `set_speed` runs first and spans [S, S + d').
493	            let grown = excess > 0 && newDuration > duration
494	            let overlapStart = max(anchor.start, start)
495	            let overlapEnd = min(anchor.end, end)
496	            guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else {
497	                problems.append(
498	                    Problem(
499	                        clip: mover.clip,
500	                        reason: "once lined up it would not play at any moment clip "
501	                            + "\(anchor.clip) plays."))
502	                continue
503	            }
504	            if delta != 0 || newDuration != duration,
505	               let hit = mover.neighbours.first(where: {
506	                   (start < $0.end && $0.start < end)
507	                       || (grown && mover.start < $0.end && $0.start < mover.start + newDuration)
508	               }) {
509	                problems.append(
510	                    Problem(
511	                        clip: mover.clip, reason: "would overlap clip \(hit.clip) on its track."))
512	                continue
513	            }
514	            synced.append(
515	                Synced(
516	                    clip: mover.clip, media: mover.media, lag: refinedTicks,
517	                    coarseLag: lagTicks, refinement: refinement, delta: delta,
518	                    start: start, confidence: found.confidence, search: found.search,
519	                    chosenBy: found.chosenBy, matchedOn: found.matchedOn,
520	                    candidates: found.candidates, drift: drift,
521	                    speed: newSpeed ?? mover.speed, duration: newDuration - excess,
522	                    correction: correction, trimmed: excess))
523	            ops += Self.ops(
524	                clip: mover.clip, delta: delta, from: mover.speed, to: newSpeed,
525	                duration: duration, newDuration: newDuration,
526	                trimTo: excess > 0 ? mover.start + excess : nil)
527	        }
528	        guard problems.isEmpty else { return .refused(problems) }
529	        return .planned(anchor: anchor.clip, synced: synced, ops: ops)
530	    }
531	
532	    /// The anchor timeline frame holding `ticks` after its zero: `⌊ticks /
533	    /// frameTicks⌋`.
534	    private static func frameIndex(_ ticks: Ticks) -> Int {
535	        let step = SyncFeatures.frameTicks
536	        let quotient = ticks / step
537	        return Int(ticks % step < 0 ? quotient - 1 : quotient)
538	    }
539	
540	    /// SY-29's fallback region: the anchor timeline frames where the two
541	    /// files (`anchorFrames` and `moverFrames` frames on their timeline
542	    /// grids) overlap at `lag`, rounded outward — `[max(0, ⌊lag⌋), min(anchorFrames,
543	    /// moverFrames + ⌈lag⌉))` — so every lag a search can score holds at
544	    /// least `minimumOverlapFrames` (a sample read past a file's end is 0).
545	    private static func filesOverlap(lag: Double, anchorFrames: Int, moverFrames: Int)
546	        -> Range<Int> {
547	        let lo = max(0, Int(lag.rounded(.down)))
548	        let hi = max(lo, min(anchorFrames, moverFrames + Int(lag.rounded(.up))))
549	        return lo..<hi
550	    }
551	}
552	import Foundation

554	/// Synchronize Audio's weak tier (road map "audio-sync-2", AS-3; spec §11
555	/// SY-18, SY-19): which planned moves were chosen only near where the mover
556	/// sits, and the words the menu's Weak match sheet and `sync_audio`'s
557	/// not-applied answer put them in.
558	///
559	/// Pure, as `AudioSync.plan` is. ONE tier decision, `weakMoves`, serves both
560	/// callers, so the menu and the tool cannot disagree about whether a plan
561	/// may apply without asking. A weak match is never applied silently — the
562	/// owner's "Unrelated clips are never moved silently" — because AS-3's
563	/// calibration showed noise near a placement reaching the z of the owner's
564	/// first pair (SY-14's stop), a pair SY-28 found to be two takes, not one
565	/// recording. A weak match is offered at all only when GCC-PHAT confirms it
566	/// (SY-29).
567	extension AudioSync {
568	
569	    /// The movers of `synced` chosen by placement (the weak tier) whose plan
570	    /// changes something — a delta, a trim or a corrected drift — in input
571	    /// order. A weak mover already in place is not asked about.
572	    static func weakMoves(_ synced: [Synced]) -> [Synced] {
573	        synced.filter { row in
574	            guard row.chosenBy == .placement else { return false }
575	            if case .apply = row.correction { return true }
576	            return row.delta != 0 || row.trimmed > 0
577	        }
578	    }
579	
580	    /// The Weak match sheet's message and detail: "Weak match: move
581	    /// “record.aifc” 0.77 s earlier (trimming 0.77 s off its head)?", then
582	    /// the anchor, each confidence and the rule it fell short of. `names` maps
583	    /// a clip id to the name the timeline shows; an id missing from it reads
584	    /// "clip N".
585	    static func weakQuestion(_ weak: [Synced], anchor: UInt32, names: [UInt32: String])
586	        -> (message: String, detail: String) {
587	        func name(_ clip: UInt32) -> String { names[clip] ?? "clip \(clip)" }
588	        let items = weak.map { row -> String in
589	            // A mover listed only for its drift correction does not move.
590	            if let speed = speedOnly(row) {
591	                return "play “\(name(row.clip))” at " + speed + ", correcting its drift"
592	            }
593	            let direction = row.delta < 0 ? "earlier" : "later"
594	            return "move “\(name(row.clip))” " + seconds(abs(row.delta)) + " s " + direction
595	                + trimming(row)
596	        }
597	        let message = "Weak match: " + items.joined(separator: "; ") + "?"
598	        let confidences = weak.map { String(format: "%.2f", $0.confidence) }
599	            .joined(separator: ", ")
600	        let detail = (weak.count == 1 ? "Its sound matches" : "Their sound matches")
601	            + " “\(name(anchor))” with confidence \(confidences): " + rule(weak.count)
602	            + " Cancel leaves everything as it is."
603	        return (message, detail)
604	    }
605	
606	    /// `sync_audio`'s note when weak moves were not applied: each move as
607	    /// the clip, its signed delta, any trim and its confidence, then the rule
608	    /// and how to apply it — once the person has agreed (SY-19).
609	    static func weakNote(_ weak: [Synced]) -> String {
610	        let items = weak.map { row -> String in
611	            if let speed = speedOnly(row) {
612	                return "clip \(row.clip) would play at " + speed + ", correcting its drift, "
613	                    + "confidence " + String(format: "%.2f", row.confidence)
614	            }
615	            let signed = String(format: "%+.2f", Double(row.delta) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
616	                .replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
617	            return "clip \(row.clip) would move by \(signed) s" + trimming(row)
618	                + ", confidence " + String(format: "%.2f", row.confidence)
619	        }
620	        return "Weak match, nothing moved: " + items.joined(separator: "; ") + " — "
621	            + rule(weak.count) + " Call sync_audio again with accept_weak: true to apply "
622	            + (weak.count == 1 ? "it" : "them") + ", once the person has agreed to "
623	            + (weak.count == 1 ? "that move." : "those moves.")
624	    }
625	
626	    // MARK: - The words
627	
628	    /// "under the 10 a match needs to apply on its own, and the best match
629	    /// within 3 s of where it sits now." — printed from the constants.
630	    private static func rule(_ count: Int) -> String {
631	        let radius = Double(Ticks(AudioSyncMatch.placementRadiusFrames) * SyncFeatures.frameTicks)
632	            / Double(ReelTime.perSecond)
633	        return "under the " + String(format: "%g", AudioSyncMatch.confidentZ)
634	            + " a match needs to apply on its own, and the best match within "
635	            + String(format: "%.0f", radius) + " s of where "
636	            + (count == 1 ? "it sits" : "each sits") + " now."
637	    }
638	
639	    /// "×1.0004" when `row` changes only its speed (no delta, no trim, its
640	    /// drift corrected), else nil.
641	    private static func speedOnly(_ row: Synced) -> String? {
642	        guard row.delta == 0, row.trimmed == 0, case .apply(let speed) = row.correction
643	        else { return nil }
644	        return "×" + String(format: "%g", speed)
645	    }
646	
647	    /// " (trimming 0.77 s off its head)" when the move trims, else "".
648	    private static func trimming(_ row: Synced) -> String {
649	        row.trimmed > 0 ? " (trimming " + seconds(row.trimmed) + " s off its head)" : ""
650	    }
651	
652	    private static func seconds(_ ticks: Ticks) -> String {
653	        String(format: "%.2f", Double(ticks) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
654	    }
655	}
656	import Foundation

658	/// Synchronize Audio's drift correction (road map "audio-sync", AS-2; spec
659	/// §11 SY-6, SY-8..SY-10): whether a measured drift is corrected, the rate
660	/// band a clip is matched within, where the corrected mover goes, how long
661	/// it becomes and in which order its two ops run.
662	///
663	/// Pure, as `AudioSync.plan` is: readings and a fitted line in, a speed, a
664	/// delta and ops out. The correction is the existing `set_speed` op with
665	/// `keep_pitch: false` (SY-6): the model keeps the rate as an f64, the plan
666	/// plays it as integer ticks over integer ticks, and `.varispeed` resamples
667	/// it with none of the time-pitch algorithm's processing.
668	extension AudioSync {
669	
670	    // MARK: - The numbers (SY-8, SY-9)
671	
672	    /// 0.2%: the furthest from ×1 a clip may play and still be matched, and
673	    /// the furthest a correction may take it.
674	    static let maximumRateDeviation = 0.002
675	    /// A drift under this, over the whole overlap, is left alone.
676	    static let minimumCorrectionMilliseconds = 5.0
677	    /// A drift must be at least this many times its own uncertainty to be
678	    /// corrected — the significance test (the owner's choice, 2026-10-15).
679	    static let minimumSignificance = 3.0
680	
681	    /// What becomes of one mover's drift: a new speed, or left as it is
682	    /// with the sentence that says why (nil when it was not measured, whose
683	    /// own note says why).
684	    enum Correction: Equatable {
685	        case apply(speed: Double)
686	        case leave(note: String?)
687	    }
688	
689	    // MARK: - Deciding (SY-8)
690	
691	    /// The correction for `drift` measured on a clip playing at `speed`, the
692	    /// three rules in SY-8's order: corrected when `|drift_ms| ≥ max(5, 3 ×
693	    /// drift_error_ms)` and the new speed stays in SY-9's band. The
694	    /// uncertainty is a test of significance, not a cap.
695	    static func correction(for drift: AudioSyncMatch.DriftAnswer, speed: Double) -> Correction {
696	        guard case .measured(let fit) = drift else { return .leave(note: nil) }
697	        if abs(fit.milliseconds) < minimumCorrectionMilliseconds {
698	            return .leave(
699	                note: "a drift of " + String(format: "%.2f", fit.milliseconds)
700	                    + " ms over the overlap is under the "
701	                    + "\(String(format: "%g", minimumCorrectionMilliseconds)) ms Synchronize "
702	                    + "Audio corrects.")
703	        }
704	        if abs(fit.milliseconds) < minimumSignificance * fit.errorMilliseconds {
705	            return .leave(
706	                note: "a drift of " + String(format: "%.2f", fit.milliseconds)
707	                    + " ms over the overlap is under "
708	                    + "\(String(format: "%g", minimumSignificance)) times its uncertainty (±"
709	                    + String(format: "%.2f", fit.errorMilliseconds) + " ms), so it cannot be "
710	                    + "told from no drift.")
711	        }
712	        let corrected = speed * (1 - fit.rate)
713	        guard inBand(corrected) else {
714	            return .leave(
715	                note: "correcting it would play the clip at ×" + String(format: "%g", corrected)
716	                    + ", beyond the 0.2% Synchronize Audio corrects.")
717	        }
718	        return .apply(speed: corrected)
719	    }
720	
721	    // MARK: - The band (SY-9)
722	
723	    /// Why a clip playing at `rate` cannot be matched; nil within the band.
724	    static func rateProblem(_ rate: Double) -> String? {
725	        guard !inBand(rate) else { return nil }
726	        return "plays at ×\(String(format: "%g", rate)); Synchronize Audio lines up clips "
727	            + "playing at ×1 or within 0.2% of it."
728	    }
729	
730	    /// Why a clip whose speed is ×1 but whose source is stretched to `rate`
731	    /// cannot be matched, even inside the band: its speed is not its rate.
732	    static func stretched(_ rate: Double) -> String {
733	        "plays at ×\(String(format: "%g", rate)) though its speed is ×1; Synchronize Audio "
734	            + "lines up clips whose speed is the rate they play at."
735	    }
736	
737	    /// Why a RAMPED clip, mover or anchor, cannot be matched (spec §11
738	    /// SR-20 (e)): the drift line assumes one rate over the clip.
739	    static let ramped = "ramps its speed (a speed action changes its rate over its length); "
740	        + "Synchronize Audio lines up clips playing at one rate."
741	
742	    /// `|rate − 1| ≤ maximumRateDeviation`, as a closed range so that the
743	    /// band's own edges (×1.002, ×0.998) are inside it in binary arithmetic.
744	    private static func inBand(_ rate: Double) -> Bool {
745	        ((1 - maximumRateDeviation)...(1 + maximumRateDeviation)).contains(rate)
746	    }
747	
748	    // MARK: - The corrected span (SY-6, SY-10)
749	
750	    /// The duration `set_speed` writes when a clip of `duration` playing at
751	    /// `old` is set to `new`: its content `round(d·old)` over `new`, snapped
752	    /// to the grid and at least one frame — the core's arithmetic without its
753	    /// hold to the file, which stays the core's backstop.
754	    static func durationAtSpeed(_ duration: Ticks, from old: Double, to new: Double, fps: Fps)
755	        -> Ticks {
756	        let content = (Double(duration) * old).rounded()
757	        let scaled = ReelTime.snapToFrame(Ticks((content / new).rounded()), fps: fps)
758	        return max(scaled, fps.frameDuration)
759	    }
760	
761	    /// The move that puts a mover set to `speed` in sync along the fitted
762	    /// line (SY-6): `set_speed` keeps its start S and in point I, so source
763	    /// tick μ plays at `S + δ + (μ − I)/s'`, which is where the anchor plays
764	    /// the same sound when `δ = zeroA + 75·c/(1 − ρ) − S + I/s'` (c in
765	    /// samples, 75 ticks each, SY-21); snapped.
766	    static func correctedDelta(
767	        anchor: Reading, mover: Reading, drift: AudioSyncMatch.Drift, speed: Double, fps: Fps
768	    ) -> Ticks {
769	        let shift = Double(AudioSyncPHAT.sampleTicks) * drift.intercept / (1 - drift.rate)
770	        let exact = Double(anchor.zero) + shift - Double(mover.start)
771	            + Double(mover.sourceIn) / speed
772	        return ReelTime.snapToFrame(Ticks(exact.rounded()), fps: fps)
773	    }
774	
775	    /// One mover's ops, each only when it changes something, ordered so
776	    /// that every span in between lies inside the old one or the final one
777	    /// (SY-10): a mover that grows moves first, one that shrinks or keeps
778	    /// its length changes speed first. A mover trimmed at its head (SY-16,
779	    /// `trimTo` the `trim_start` target S + e) changes speed first, so the
780	    /// trim advances its in point at the new speed, then trims, then moves.
781	    static func ops(
782	        clip: UInt32, delta: Ticks, from old: Double, to new: Double?, duration: Ticks,
783	        newDuration: Ticks, trimTo: Ticks? = nil
784	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
785	        let move: ReelOp? = delta != 0 ? ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [clip], delta: delta) : nil
786	        var speed: ReelOp?
787	        if let new = new, new != old {
788	            speed = ReelOp.setSpeed(clip: clip, rate: new, keepPitch: false)
789	        }
790	        if let trimTo {
791	            return [speed, ReelOp.trimStart(clip: clip, to: trimTo), move].compactMap { $0 }
792	        }
793	        if newDuration > duration {
794	            return [move, speed].compactMap { $0 }
795	        }
796	        return [speed, move].compactMap { $0 }
797	    }
798	}
799	import Foundation
800	
801	/// Where Synchronize Audio's one GCC-PHAT refinement runs (#302; spec §11
802	/// SY-32, amending SY-20's and SY-29's centred region): moved out of
803	/// `AudioSync.swift`, where the region was the overlap's centre 30 s.
804	///
805	/// It is pure, as `plan` is: an overlap, the two readings' timeline-grid
806	/// features and masks and the line in, a range of anchor timeline samples
807	/// out. It only chooses WHERE: the refinement, its z and the gate are
808	/// `AudioSyncPHAT`'s and `plan`'s (SY-29), and there is still one region.
809	extension AudioSync {
810	
811	    /// SY-32's region: `overlap` (anchor timeline frames) ×128, in anchor
812	    /// timeline samples, when it holds at most W = `maximumRegionSamples /
813	    /// hop` frames; else the W frames whose features agree most along
814	    /// `line`. Frame f scores `Σ_k A[f, k]·M[m(f), k]`, A and M the features
815	    /// `standardised` as the match was (over the speech frames when it
816	    /// matched on speech), `m(f) = f − round((c + ρ·128f)/128)`, and 0 when
817	    /// f or m(f) lies outside its file. The start s in `[lo, hi − W]` with
818	    /// the greatest summed score wins; the centred start `⌊(lo + hi)/2⌋ −
819	    /// ⌊W/2⌋` is the first candidate, replaced only by a strictly greater
820	    /// sum or an equal one nearer it.
821	    static func refinementRegion(
822	        overlap: Range<Int>, anchorFrames: [Float], moverFrames: [Float], anchorSpeech: [Bool]?,
823	        moverSpeech: [Bool]?, matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn, line: AudioSyncPHAT.Line
824	    ) -> Range<Int> {
825	        let hop = SyncFeatures.hop
826	        let span = AudioSyncPHAT.maximumRegionSamples / hop
827	        let lo = overlap.lowerBound
828	        let hi = overlap.upperBound
829	        guard overlap.count > span else { return (lo * hop)..<(hi * hop) }
830	
831	        let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
832	        let onSpeech = matchedOn == .speech
833	        let a = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(anchorFrames, speech: onSpeech ? anchorSpeech : nil)
834	        let m = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(moverFrames, speech: onSpeech ? moverSpeech : nil)
835	        let anchorCount = a.count / width
836	        let moverCount = m.count / width
837	
838	        // prefix[i] = Σ score over the overlap's first i frames.
839	        var prefix = [Double](repeating: 0, count: overlap.count + 1)
840	        a.withUnsafeBufferPointer { anchor in
841	            m.withUnsafeBufferPointer { mover in
842	                for (index, f) in overlap.enumerated() {
843	                    let lag = ((line.intercept + line.rate * Double(f * hop)) / Double(hop))
844	                        .rounded()
845	                    let g = f - Int(lag)
846	                    var score = 0.0
847	                    if f >= 0, f < anchorCount, g >= 0, g < moverCount {
848	                        let x = f * width
849	                        let y = g * width
850	                        for k in 0..<width { score += Double(anchor[x + k]) * Double(mover[y + k]) }
851	                    }
852	                    prefix[index + 1] = prefix[index] + score
853	                }
854	            }
855	        }
856	        func sum(_ start: Int) -> Double { prefix[start - lo + span] - prefix[start - lo] }
857	
858	        let last = hi - span
859	        let centred = min(max(lo, (lo + hi) / 2 - span / 2), last)
860	        var best = centred
861	        var bestSum = sum(centred)
862	        for start in lo...last {
863	            let value = sum(start)
864	            if value > bestSum || (value == bestSum && abs(start - centred) < abs(best - centred)) {
865	                best = start
866	                bestSum = value
867	            }
868	        }
869	        return (best * hop)..<((best + span) * hop)
870	    }
871	}
