1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio and `sync_audio` (road maps "audio-sync", AS-1 and
4	/// AS-2, and "audio-sync-2", AS-3 and AS-4; spec §11 SY-1..SY-21): selected clips that
5	/// play sound are lined up by their sound. One ANCHOR stays where it is and every other clip moves by a
6	/// frame-snapped `move_clip`, its clock drift corrected by a `set_speed`, all
7	/// as one undo step — or the whole command refuses, naming every reason at
8	/// once (SY-1).
9	///
10	/// `AudioNormalize`'s shape: `read` takes everything off the document once
11	/// (the edited project's snapshot and plan, and each file's cached sync
12	/// features, samples and speech probabilities), and `plan` is pure — readings
13	/// in, ops or a refusal out. The menu item and the tool call the same pair,
14	/// so neither measures anything of its own. The signal arithmetic is
15	/// `AudioSyncMatch`'s, the sub-frame refinement `AudioSyncPHAT`'s (SY-20),
16	/// where to look and what to choose
17	/// `AudioSync+Search.swift`'s, and which planned moves are only WEAK — asked
18	/// about, never applied silently (SY-18, SY-19) — `AudioSync+Weak.swift`'s.
19	///
20	/// **Time.** A reading's `zero` is the project tick at which its file's
21	/// source tick 0 would play (`segment.start − round(segment.sourceIn /
22	/// speed)`), and its features are resampled onto its timeline grid (frame k
23	/// = source frame k·speed; themselves at ×1), and so are its speech masks
24	/// (SY-17, frame k = source frame round(k·speed)), so a sound at timeline
25	/// frame `f` plays at `zero + f·9600`; its samples are read at `t·speed`
26	/// where they are used (SY-20). A mover whose sound at frame `m` is the
27	/// anchor's at `m + lag` lines up when its zero becomes `zeroA + lag·9600`:
28	/// `delta = zeroA − zeroN + lag·9600`, snapped to the frame grid (SY-4),
29	/// because the model stores no sub-frame time.
30	///
31	/// **Drift and the refinement** (SY-6, SY-20, SY-21, SY-29). Over the overlap
32	/// the coarse delta gives, the lag is fitted as a line, `lag(a) = c + ρ·a` (a
33	/// an anchor timeline sample, 75 ticks each, c in samples); not measured, the
34	/// line is the coarse lag. PHAT along it over the 30 s of the overlap whose
35	/// features agree most (SY-32) — the files' overlap at the lag when that played
36	/// overlap is under 2 s — shifts c by a clear peak's sub-sample shift. **The
37	/// waveform gate** (SY-29): a match of either tier stands only on that clear
38	/// peak; a peak that is not clear refuses the command (`incoherent`), and so
39	/// does a refinement that cannot run (`unconfirmed`) unless neither reading
40	/// carries samples at all, when the features' tier stands. Corrected
41	/// (SY-8), the mover's speed becomes `s' = s·(1 − ρ)` and, since `set_speed`
42	/// keeps its start S and in point I, source tick μ plays at `S + δ + (μ −
43	/// I)/s'` — on the anchor's line everywhere when `δ = snapToFrame(round(zeroA
44	/// + 75·c/(1 − ρ) − S + I/s'))` (`correctedDelta`). Left uncorrected, it is
45	/// placed by the line's value at the overlap's centre aMid, `delta =
46	/// snapToFrame(zeroA − zeroN + round((c + ρ·aMid)·75))`; not measured, by
47	/// the (refined) lag. Snapping leaves one constant offset of at most half a
48	/// frame.
49	///
50	/// **The head trim** (SY-16, the owner's choice): a mover that would start
51	/// before 0 loses the excess off its head by a `trim_start` between the
52	/// `set_speed` and the `move_clip`, so it starts at 0 and what remains plays
53	/// in sync. **What it refuses rather than lets the core decide** (SY-4):
54	/// `move_clip` clamps the earliest clip at 0, and on an overlap within the
55	/// overlap rule it ADDS a cross dissolve instead of refusing — so a mover
56	/// that would land on another clip of its own track is refused here, by
57	/// name — on the FINAL span, after any change of speed or trim (SY-10).
58	enum AudioSync {
59	
60	    // MARK: - Vocabulary
61	
62	    /// One reason the command will not run: about a clip ("clip N: …") or
63	    /// about the selection as a whole (the reason alone).
64	    struct Problem: Equatable {
65	        let clip: UInt32?
66	        let reason: String
67	
68	        var description: String {
69	            guard let clip = clip else { return reason }
70	            return "clip \(clip): \(reason)"
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    /// Another top-level clip on a reading's track, as the span it occupies.
75	    struct Neighbour: Equatable {
76	        let clip: UInt32
77	        let start: Ticks
78	        let end: Ticks
79	    }
80	
81	    /// One clip that can be matched: where it sits, where its file's tick 0
82	    /// plays, whether it has pictures (the anchor rule, SY-2), its file's
83	    /// samples and sync features, and the clips it shares its track with.
84	    struct Reading: Equatable {
85	        let clip: UInt32
86	        let media: UInt32
87	        let trackIndex: Int
88	        let start: Ticks
89	        let end: Ticks
90	        let zero: Ticks
91	        let hasVideo: Bool
92	        /// Its file's 8 kHz samples (`cache/sync/<id>.pcm`) on the SOURCE grid.
93	        let samples: [Int16]
94	        /// Its file's `SyncFeatures` frames on the SOURCE grid, frame-major.
95	        let features: [Float]
96	        /// Which of those frames are speech (SY-17), one per frame on the
97	        /// SOURCE grid; nil when the voice model cannot be used.
98	        let speech: [Bool]?
99	        let neighbours: [Neighbour]
100	        /// The clip's playback rate, within SY-9's band.
101	        let speed: Double
102	        /// Its first audio segment's in point, in source ticks.
103	        let sourceIn: Ticks
104	    }
105	
106	    /// Everything a run reads, taken off the document once.
107	    struct Input {
108	        let readings: [Reading]
109	        let problems: [Problem]
110	        /// The anchor the caller named, or nil for SY-2's rule.
111	        let anchor: UInt32?
112	        let fps: Fps
113	    }
114	
115	    /// One mover's answer: its lag in ticks (refined, at the overlap's
116	    /// centre), the coarse lag and the refinement (SY-20), the frame-snapped
117	    /// move, where it lands, how sure the match was and how it was found,
118	    /// what drift it measured, its speed, duration and correction after the
119	    /// command, and the head it lost to start at 0 (SY-16).
120	    struct Synced: Equatable {
121	        let clip: UInt32
122	        let media: UInt32
123	        let lag: Ticks
124	        /// The coarse match's lag in ticks, before the refinement.
125	        let coarseLag: Ticks
126	        /// The PHAT refinement over the overlap; nil when none ran.
127	        let refinement: AudioSyncPHAT.Refinement?
128	        let delta: Ticks
129	        let start: Ticks
130	        /// The chosen lag's z-score (SY-12).
131	        let confidence: Double
132	        let search: Search
133	        let chosenBy: ChosenBy
134	        let matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn
135	        let candidates: [CandidateMove]
136	        let drift: AudioSyncMatch.DriftAnswer
137	        let speed: Double
138	        let duration: Ticks
139	        let correction: Correction
140	        let trimmed: Ticks
141	    }
142	
143	    enum Plan {
144	        case refused([Problem])
145	        case planned(anchor: UInt32, synced: [Synced], ops: [ReelOp])
146	    }
147	
148	    // MARK: - Offering it
149	
150	    /// Whether the command can be offered: at least two selected clips pass
151	    /// `AudioNormalize.canOffer` (sound, and not a nest). A cheap pre-check
152	    /// of the snapshot, never the plan — `read` may still refuse.
153	    static func canOffer(_ clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
154	        clips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }.count >= 2
155	    }
156	
157	    // MARK: - Reading
158	
159	    /// Reads the edited project's snapshot, plan, sync features and samples
160	    /// and (with the voice model) speech probabilities for `clips` (nil:
161	    /// the document's selection). nil only when the plan cannot be read; a
162	    /// clip that cannot be matched is a `Problem`.
163	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]?, anchor: UInt32?)
164	        -> Input? {
165	        guard let plan = document.editedProject.plan else { return nil }
166	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
167	
168	        var audio: [UInt32: [PlanSegment]] = [:]
169	        for track in plan.audioTracks {
170	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
171	                audio[segment.clip, default: []].append(segment)
172	            }
173	        }
174	        var pictured: Set<UInt32> = []
175	        for track in plan.videoTracks {
176	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
177	                pictured.insert(segment.clip)
178	            }
179	        }
180	
181	        var samplesByMedia: [UInt32: [Int16]] = [:]
182	        var featuresByMedia: [UInt32: [Float]] = [:]
183	        var speechByMedia: [UInt32: [Float]] = [:]
184	        let voice = SileroVAD.isAvailable
185	        var readings: [Reading] = []
186	        var problems: [Problem] = []
187	        var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
188	        for id in clips ?? document.selection.sorted() where seen.insert(id).inserted {
189	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else {
190	                problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: "is not a clip in this project."))
191	                continue
192	            }
193	            if case .nest = clip.source {
194	                problems.append(
195	                    Problem(
196	                        clip: id,
197	                        reason: "is a nest, and a nest has no sound of its own to match: the "
198	                            + "waveform cache is per media file and the clips inside a nest "
199	                            + "each have their own. Open it (⌘↓) and synchronize the clips "
200	                            + "inside."))
201	                continue
202	            }
203	            // A ramp's rate changes over the clip, and the drift line reads
204	            // one (spec §11 SR-20 (e)); the map is the snapshot's handle's.
205	            if document.editedProject.sourceMap(id)?.ramped == true {
206	                problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: AudioSync.ramped))
207	                continue
208	            }
209	            guard let segments = audio[id]?.sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }),
210	                  let first = segments.first
211	            else {
212	                problems.append(
213	                    Problem(
214	                        clip: id,
215	                        reason: "plays no sound in this timeline, so there is nothing to line "
216	                            + "it up by. A still, a clip whose media has no audio track and a "
217	                            + "clip with audio switched off all read this way."))
218	                continue
219	            }
220	            if clip.speed != 1 || segments.contains(where: { $0.isTimeScaled }) {
221	                let scaled = segments.first { $0.isTimeScaled } ?? first
222	                let rate = clip.speed != 1
223	                    ? clip.speed : Double(scaled.sourceDuration) / Double(max(scaled.duration, 1))
224	                // At speed 1 a time-scaled segment is a stretch the clip's
225	                // speed does not say, so neither `zero` nor `set_speed` can
226	                // read it: refused, as AS-1 did (SY-9).
227	                if let problem = rateProblem(rate) ?? (clip.speed == 1 ? stretched(rate) : nil) {
228	                    problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: problem))
229	                    continue
230	                }
231	            }
232	            if case .media(_, _, true) = clip.source {
233	                problems.append(
234	                    Problem(
235	                        clip: id,
236	                        reason: "plays reversed; Synchronize Audio lines up clips playing "
237	                            + "forwards."))
238	                continue
239	            }
240	            let cached = featuresByMedia[first.media] ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
241	                MediaImporter.loadSyncFeatures(for: first.media, in: $0)
242	            }
243	            let probabilities = !voice ? nil : speechByMedia[first.media]
244	                ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
245	                    MediaImporter.loadSpeech(for: first.media, in: $0)
246	                }
247	            let pcm = samplesByMedia[first.media] ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
248	                MediaImporter.loadSyncSamples(for: first.media, in: $0)
249	            }
250	            // The samples are the features' own: a count that disagrees is a
251	            // pass not finished, read as not written.
252	            let written = cached.flatMap { features in
253	                pcm.flatMap {
254	                    SyncFeatures.frameCount(samples: $0.count)
255	                        == features.count / SyncFeatures.coefficients ? $0 : nil
256	                }
257	            }
258	            guard let features = cached, let samples = written, !voice || probabilities != nil
259	            else {
260	                // The waveform can be on the timeline while the features
261	                // and speech that land after it are not: say which.
262	                let missing = written == nil
263	                    ? " for Synchronize Audio — its sound features have not been written yet."
264	                    : " for Synchronize Audio — its speech has not been detected yet."
265	                problems.append(
266	                    Problem(
267	                        clip: id,
268	                        reason: "is still being analysed" + missing + " Try again in a moment."))
269	                continue
270	            }
271	            featuresByMedia[first.media] = features
272	            samplesByMedia[first.media] = samples
273	            if let probabilities { speechByMedia[first.media] = probabilities }
274	            let frames = features.count / SyncFeatures.coefficients
275	            guard frames >= AudioSyncMatch.minimumStretchFrames else {
276	                let seconds = String(
277	                    format: "%g",
278	                    Double(Ticks(AudioSyncMatch.minimumStretchFrames) * SyncFeatures.frameTicks)
279	                        / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
280	                problems.append(
281	                    Problem(
282	                        clip: id,
283	                        reason: "is too short to match: its file holds under \(seconds) s of "
284	                            + "sound."))
285	                continue
286	            }
287	            let neighbours = snapshot.clips
288	                .filter { $0.track == clip.track && $0.id != id }
289	                .map { Neighbour(clip: $0.id, start: $0.start, end: $0.start + $0.duration) }
290	            readings.append(
291	                Reading(
292	                    clip: id, media: first.media,
293	                    trackIndex: snapshot.tracks.firstIndex { $0.id == clip.track } ?? 0,
294	                    start: clip.start, end: clip.start + clip.duration,
295	                    zero: first.start - Ticks((Double(first.sourceIn) / clip.speed).rounded()),
296	                    hasVideo: pictured.contains(id), samples: samples, features: features,
297	                    speech: probabilities.map { AudioSyncMatch.speechMask($0, frames: frames) },
298	                    neighbours: neighbours,
299	                    speed: clip.speed, sourceIn: first.sourceIn))
300	        }
301	        return Input(
302	            readings: readings, problems: problems, anchor: anchor, fps: snapshot.canvas.fps)
303	    }
304	
305	    // MARK: - The anchor (SY-2)
306	
307	    /// The named reading; else, among the readings with pictures (all of them
308	    /// when none has), the earliest start, then the rearmost track, then the
309	    /// lowest id.
310	    static func chooseAnchor(_ readings: [Reading], named: UInt32?) -> Reading? {
311	        if let named = named { return readings.first { $0.clip == named } }
312	        let pictured = readings.filter { $0.hasVideo }
313	        let pool = pictured.isEmpty ? readings : pictured
314	        return pool.min { a, b in
315	            if a.start != b.start { return a.start < b.start }
316	            if a.trackIndex != b.trackIndex { return a.trackIndex < b.trackIndex }
317	            return a.clip < b.clip
318	        }
319	    }
320	
321	    // MARK: - Planning (SY-1, SY-4, SY-6..SY-10, SY-12..SY-16)
322	
323	    /// The ops, or every reason there are none. All or nothing: one problem
324	    /// anywhere refuses the whole command.
325	    static func plan(_ input: Input) -> Plan {
326	        guard input.problems.isEmpty else { return .refused(input.problems) }
327	        let readings = input.readings
328	        guard readings.count >= 2 else {
329	            return .refused([
330	                Problem(clip: nil, reason: "Synchronize Audio needs at least two clips with sound.")
331	            ])
332	        }
333	        guard let anchor = chooseAnchor(readings, named: input.anchor) else {
334	            return .refused([
335	                Problem(
336	                    clip: input.anchor,
337	                    reason: "is not one of the clips being synchronized, so it cannot be the "
338	                        + "anchor.")
339	            ])
340	        }
341	
342	        var problems: [Problem] = []
343	        var byTrack: [Int: [UInt32]] = [:]
344	        for reading in readings { byTrack[reading.trackIndex, default: []].append(reading.clip) }
345	        for index in byTrack.keys.sorted() {
346	            guard let ids = byTrack[index], ids.count > 1 else { continue }
347	            let names = ids.map { "clip \($0)" }.joined(separator: " and ")
348	            problems.append(
349	                Problem(
350	                    clip: nil,
351	                    reason: "\(names) are on one track; Synchronize Audio lines up clips on "
352	                        + "different tracks."))
353	        }
354	
355	        // A file with no sound cannot be matched; the problem is the silent
356	        // clip's own, so a silent anchor is named once, not on every mover.
357	        let silent = "has no sound to line up by."
358	        let anchorSilent = AudioSyncMatch.isSilent(anchor.features)
359	        if anchorSilent { problems.append(Problem(clip: anchor.clip, reason: silent)) }
360	        let anchorFrames = AudioSyncMatch.resampledFrames(anchor.features, speed: anchor.speed)
361	        let anchorSpeech = anchor.speech.map {
362	            AudioSyncMatch.resampledMask($0, speed: anchor.speed)
363	        }
364	
365	        let hop = Double(SyncFeatures.hop)
366	        let sample = Double(AudioSyncPHAT.sampleTicks)
367	        // SY-22: one setup for every refinement this plan makes.
368	        let fft = AudioSyncPHAT.FFT(log2n: AudioSyncPHAT.planLog2n)
369	        var synced: [Synced] = []
370	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
371	        for mover in readings where mover.clip != anchor.clip {
372	            guard !AudioSyncMatch.isSilent(mover.features) else {
373	                problems.append(Problem(clip: mover.clip, reason: silent))
374	                continue
375	            }
376	            if anchorSilent { continue }
377	            let moverFrames = AudioSyncMatch.resampledFrames(mover.features, speed: mover.speed)
378	            let moverSpeech = mover.speech.map {
379	                AudioSyncMatch.resampledMask($0, speed: mover.speed)
380	            }
381	            let found: Found
382	            switch find(
383	                anchor: anchor, anchorFrames: anchorFrames, anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech,
384	                mover: mover, moverFrames: moverFrames, moverSpeech: moverSpeech, fps: input.fps)
385	            {
386	            case .refused(let problem):
387	                problems.append(problem)
388	                continue
389	            case .found(let answer):
390	                found = answer
391	            }
392	            let lagTicks = Ticks((found.lag * Double(SyncFeatures.frameTicks)).rounded())
393	            let coarse = ReelTime.snapToFrame(anchor.zero - mover.zero + lagTicks, fps: input.fps)
394	            let lower = frameIndex(max(anchor.start, mover.start + coarse) - anchor.zero)
395	            let upper = frameIndex(min(anchor.end, mover.end + coarse) - anchor.zero)
396	            let window = max(0, lower)..<max(0, lower, upper)
397	            var drift = AudioSyncMatch.drift(
398	                anchor: anchorFrames, mover: moverFrames, anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech,
399	                moverSpeech: moverSpeech, anchorSamples: anchor.samples,
400	                moverSamples: mover.samples, anchorSpeed: anchor.speed, moverSpeed: mover.speed,
401	                lag: found.lag, overlap: window, fft: fft)
402	            // SY-20: PHAT along the line over 30 s of the overlap (SY-32); under
403	            // 2 s played, over the files' overlap at the lag instead (SY-29).
404	            var line = AudioSyncPHAT.Line(intercept: found.lag * hop, rate: 0)
405	            if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
406	                line = AudioSyncPHAT.Line(intercept: fit.intercept, rate: fit.rate)
407	            }
408	            let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
409	            let played = refinementRegion(
410	                overlap: window, anchorFrames: anchorFrames, moverFrames: moverFrames,
411	                anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech, moverSpeech: moverSpeech, matchedOn: found.matchedOn,
412	                line: line)
413	            let reach = played.count >= AudioSyncPHAT.minimumRegionSamples
414	                ? played
415	                : refinementRegion(
416	                    overlap: filesOverlap(
417	                        lag: found.lag, anchorFrames: anchorFrames.count / width,
418	                        moverFrames: moverFrames.count / width),
419	                    anchorFrames: anchorFrames, moverFrames: moverFrames,
420	                    anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech, moverSpeech: moverSpeech,
421	                    matchedOn: found.matchedOn, line: line)
422	            let refinement = AudioSyncPHAT.refine(
423	                anchor: anchor.samples, anchorSpeed: anchor.speed, mover: mover.samples,
424	                moverSpeed: mover.speed, line: line, region: reach, fft: fft)
425	            // SY-29, the waveform gate: either tier stands only on a clear
426	            // peak; a refinement that could not run refuses too, unless
427	            // neither reading carries samples at all.
428	            if let refinement, !refinement.clear {
429	                problems.append(
430	                    Problem(
431	                        clip: nil,
432	                        reason: incoherent(
433	                            anchor: anchor.clip, mover: mover.clip, delta: coarse,
434	                            confidence: found.confidence, refinement: refinement)))
435	                continue
436	            }
437	            if refinement == nil, !(anchor.samples.isEmpty && mover.samples.isEmpty) {
438	                problems.append(
439	                    Problem(
440	                        clip: nil,
441	                        reason: unconfirmed(
442	                            anchor: anchor.clip, mover: mover.clip, delta: coarse,
443	                            confidence: found.confidence)))
444	                continue
445	            }
446	            var refinedTicks = lagTicks
447	            var delta = coarse
448	            if let refinement, refinement.clear {
449	                if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
450	                    drift = .measured(
451	                        AudioSyncMatch.Drift(
452	                            ppm: fit.ppm, milliseconds: fit.milliseconds, rate: fit.rate,
453	                            intercept: fit.intercept + refinement.shift,
454	                            errorMilliseconds: fit.errorMilliseconds, windows: fit.windows,
455	                            on: fit.on))
456	                } else {
457	                    refinedTicks = Ticks(((found.lag * hop + refinement.shift) * sample).rounded())
458	                    delta = ReelTime.snapToFrame(
459	                        anchor.zero - mover.zero + refinedTicks, fps: input.fps)
460	                }
461	            }
462	            let correction = Self.correction(for: drift, speed: mover.speed)
463	            var newSpeed: Double?
464	            if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
465	                let centre = Double(window.lowerBound + window.upperBound) / 2 * hop
466	                let line = Ticks(((fit.intercept + fit.rate * centre) * sample).rounded())
467	                refinedTicks = line
468	                delta = ReelTime.snapToFrame(anchor.zero - mover.zero + line, fps: input.fps)
469	                if case .apply(let speed) = correction {
470	                    newSpeed = speed
471	                    delta = correctedDelta(
472	                        anchor: anchor, mover: mover, drift: fit, speed: speed, fps: input.fps)
473	                }
474	            }
475	            let duration = mover.end - mover.start
476	            let newDuration = newSpeed.map {
477	                durationAtSpeed(duration, from: mover.speed, to: $0, fps: input.fps)
478	            } ?? duration
479	            // SY-16: what would fall before 0 is trimmed off the mover's head.
480	            let excess = max(0, -(mover.start + delta))
481	            let start = mover.start + delta + excess
482	            let end = mover.start + delta + newDuration
483	            guard newDuration - excess >= input.fps.frameDuration else {
484	                let seconds = Double(excess) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond)
485	                problems.append(
486	                    Problem(
487	                        clip: mover.clip,
488	                        reason: "would have to lose " + String(format: "%.2f", seconds)
489	                            + " s of its head to start at 0, leaving under a frame of it."))
490	                continue
491	            }
492	            // Corrected and growing, `set_speed` runs first and spans [S, S + d').
493	            let grown = excess > 0 && newDuration > duration
494	            let overlapStart = max(anchor.start, start)
495	            let overlapEnd = min(anchor.end, end)
496	            guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else {
497	                problems.append(
498	                    Problem(
499	                        clip: mover.clip,
500	                        reason: "once lined up it would not play at any moment clip "
501	                            + "\(anchor.clip) plays."))
502	                continue
503	            }
504	            if delta != 0 || newDuration != duration,
505	               let hit = mover.neighbours.first(where: {
506	                   (start < $0.end && $0.start < end)
507	                       || (grown && mover.start < $0.end && $0.start < mover.start + newDuration)
508	               }) {
509	                problems.append(
510	                    Problem(
511	                        clip: mover.clip, reason: "would overlap clip \(hit.clip) on its track."))
512	                continue
513	            }
514	            synced.append(
515	                Synced(
516	                    clip: mover.clip, media: mover.media, lag: refinedTicks,
517	                    coarseLag: lagTicks, refinement: refinement, delta: delta,
518	                    start: start, confidence: found.confidence, search: found.search,
519	                    chosenBy: found.chosenBy, matchedOn: found.matchedOn,
520	                    candidates: found.candidates, drift: drift,
521	                    speed: newSpeed ?? mover.speed, duration: newDuration - excess,
522	                    correction: correction, trimmed: excess))
523	            ops += Self.ops(

557	/// not-applied answer put them in.
558	///

560	/// callers, so the menu and the tool cannot disagree about whether a plan
561	/// may apply without asking. A weak match is never applied silently — the
562	/// owner's "Unrelated clips are never moved silently" — because AS-3's
563	/// calibration showed noise near a placement reaching the z of the owner's
564	/// first pair (SY-14's stop), a pair SY-28 found to be two takes, not one
565	/// recording. A weak match is offered at all only when GCC-PHAT confirms it
566	/// (SY-29).
567	extension AudioSync {
568	
569	    /// The movers of `synced` chosen by placement (the weak tier) whose plan
570	    /// changes something — a delta, a trim or a corrected drift — in input
571	    /// order. A weak mover already in place is not asked about.
572	    static func weakMoves(_ synced: [Synced]) -> [Synced] {
573	        synced.filter { row in
574	            guard row.chosenBy == .placement else { return false }
575	            if case .apply = row.correction { return true }
576	            return row.delta != 0 || row.trimmed > 0
577	        }
578	    }

580	    /// The Weak match sheet's message and detail: "Weak match: move
581	    /// “record.aifc” 0.77 s earlier (trimming 0.77 s off its head)?", then
582	    /// the anchor, each confidence and the rule it fell short of. `names` maps
583	    /// a clip id to the name the timeline shows; an id missing from it reads
584	    /// "clip N".
585	    static func weakQuestion(_ weak: [Synced], anchor: UInt32, names: [UInt32: String])
586	        -> (message: String, detail: String) {
587	        func name(_ clip: UInt32) -> String { names[clip] ?? "clip \(clip)" }
588	        let items = weak.map { row -> String in
589	            // A mover listed only for its drift correction does not move.
590	            if let speed = speedOnly(row) {
591	                return "play “\(name(row.clip))” at " + speed + ", correcting its drift"
592	            }
593	            let direction = row.delta < 0 ? "earlier" : "later"
594	            return "move “\(name(row.clip))” " + seconds(abs(row.delta)) + " s " + direction
595	                + trimming(row)
596	        }
597	        let message = "Weak match: " + items.joined(separator: "; ") + "?"
598	        let confidences = weak.map { String(format: "%.2f", $0.confidence) }
599	            .joined(separator: ", ")
600	        let detail = (weak.count == 1 ? "Its sound matches" : "Their sound matches")
601	            + " “\(name(anchor))” with confidence \(confidences): " + rule(weak.count)

608	    /// and how to apply it — once the person has agreed (SY-19).
609	    static func weakNote(_ weak: [Synced]) -> String {
610	        let items = weak.map { row -> String in
611	            if let speed = speedOnly(row) {
612	                return "clip \(row.clip) would play at " + speed + ", correcting its drift, "

616	                .replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")

618	                + ", confidence " + String(format: "%.2f", row.confidence)

649	        row.trimmed > 0 ? " (trimming " + seconds(row.trimmed) + " s off its head)" : ""

654	    }

658	/// Synchronize Audio's drift correction (road map "audio-sync", AS-2; spec
659	/// §11 SY-6, SY-8..SY-10): whether a measured drift is corrected, the rate
660	/// band a clip is matched within, where the corrected mover goes, how long
661	/// it becomes and in which order its two ops run.
662	///
663	/// Pure, as `AudioSync.plan` is: readings and a fitted line in, a speed, a
664	/// delta and ops out. The correction is the existing `set_speed` op with
665	/// `keep_pitch: false` (SY-6): the model keeps the rate as an f64, the plan
666	/// plays it as integer ticks over integer ticks, and `.varispeed` resamples
667	/// it with none of the time-pitch algorithm's processing.
668	extension AudioSync {
669	
670	    // MARK: - The numbers (SY-8, SY-9)
671	
672	    /// 0.2%: the furthest from ×1 a clip may play and still be matched, and
673	    /// the furthest a correction may take it.
674	    static let maximumRateDeviation = 0.002
675	    /// A drift under this, over the whole overlap, is left alone.
676	    static let minimumCorrectionMilliseconds = 5.0
677	    /// A drift must be at least this many times its own uncertainty to be
678	    /// corrected — the significance test (the owner's choice, 2026-10-15).
679	    static let minimumSignificance = 3.0
680	
681	    /// What becomes of one mover's drift: a new speed, or left as it is
682	    /// with the sentence that says why (nil when it was not measured, whose
683	    /// own note says why).
684	    enum Correction: Equatable {
685	        case apply(speed: Double)
686	        case leave(note: String?)
687	    }
688	
689	    // MARK: - Deciding (SY-8)
690	
691	    /// The correction for `drift` measured on a clip playing at `speed`, the
692	    /// three rules in SY-8's order: corrected when `|drift_ms| ≥ max(5, 3 ×
693	    /// drift_error_ms)` and the new speed stays in SY-9's band. The
694	    /// uncertainty is a test of significance, not a cap.
695	    static func correction(for drift: AudioSyncMatch.DriftAnswer, speed: Double) -> Correction {
696	        guard case .measured(let fit) = drift else { return .leave(note: nil) }
697	        if abs(fit.milliseconds) < minimumCorrectionMilliseconds {
698	            return .leave(
699	                note: "a drift of " + String(format: "%.2f", fit.milliseconds)
700	                    + " ms over the overlap is under the "
701	                    + "\(String(format: "%g", minimumCorrectionMilliseconds)) ms Synchronize "
702	                    + "Audio corrects.")
703	        }
704	        if abs(fit.milliseconds) < minimumSignificance * fit.errorMilliseconds {
705	            return .leave(
706	                note: "a drift of " + String(format: "%.2f", fit.milliseconds)
707	                    + " ms over the overlap is under "
708	                    + "\(String(format: "%g", minimumSignificance)) times its uncertainty (±"
709	                    + String(format: "%.2f", fit.errorMilliseconds) + " ms), so it cannot be "
710	                    + "told from no drift.")
711	        }
712	        let corrected = speed * (1 - fit.rate)
713	        guard inBand(corrected) else {
714	            return .leave(
715	                note: "correcting it would play the clip at ×" + String(format: "%g", corrected)
716	                    + ", beyond the 0.2% Synchronize Audio corrects.")
717	        }
718	        return .apply(speed: corrected)
719	    }
720	
721	    // MARK: - The band (SY-9)
722	
723	    /// Why a clip playing at `rate` cannot be matched; nil within the band.
724	    static func rateProblem(_ rate: Double) -> String? {
725	        guard !inBand(rate) else { return nil }
726	        return "plays at ×\(String(format: "%g", rate)); Synchronize Audio lines up clips "
727	            + "playing at ×1 or within 0.2% of it."
728	    }
729	
730	    /// Why a clip whose speed is ×1 but whose source is stretched to `rate`
731	    /// cannot be matched, even inside the band: its speed is not its rate.
732	    static func stretched(_ rate: Double) -> String {
733	        "plays at ×\(String(format: "%g", rate)) though its speed is ×1; Synchronize Audio "
734	            + "lines up clips whose speed is the rate they play at."
735	    }
736	
737	    /// Why a RAMPED clip, mover or anchor, cannot be matched (spec §11
738	    /// SR-20 (e)): the drift line assumes one rate over the clip.
739	    static let ramped = "ramps its speed (a speed action changes its rate over its length); "
740	        + "Synchronize Audio lines up clips playing at one rate."
741	
742	    /// `|rate − 1| ≤ maximumRateDeviation`, as a closed range so that the
743	    /// band's own edges (×1.002, ×0.998) are inside it in binary arithmetic.
744	    private static func inBand(_ rate: Double) -> Bool {
745	        ((1 - maximumRateDeviation)...(1 + maximumRateDeviation)).contains(rate)
746	    }
747	
748	    // MARK: - The corrected span (SY-6, SY-10)
749	
750	    /// The duration `set_speed` writes when a clip of `duration` playing at
751	    /// `old` is set to `new`: its content `round(d·old)` over `new`, snapped
752	    /// to the grid and at least one frame — the core's arithmetic without its
753	    /// hold to the file, which stays the core's backstop.
754	    static func durationAtSpeed(_ duration: Ticks, from old: Double, to new: Double, fps: Fps)
755	        -> Ticks {
756	        let content = (Double(duration) * old).rounded()
757	        let scaled = ReelTime.snapToFrame(Ticks((content / new).rounded()), fps: fps)
758	        return max(scaled, fps.frameDuration)
759	    }
760	
761	    /// The move that puts a mover set to `speed` in sync along the fitted
762	    /// line (SY-6): `set_speed` keeps its start S and in point I, so source
763	    /// tick μ plays at `S + δ + (μ − I)/s'`, which is where the anchor plays
764	    /// the same sound when `δ = zeroA + 75·c/(1 − ρ) − S + I/s'` (c in
765	    /// samples, 75 ticks each, SY-21); snapped.
766	    static func correctedDelta(
767	        anchor: Reading, mover: Reading, drift: AudioSyncMatch.Drift, speed: Double, fps: Fps
768	    ) -> Ticks {
769	        let shift = Double(AudioSyncPHAT.sampleTicks) * drift.intercept / (1 - drift.rate)
770	        let exact = Double(anchor.zero) + shift - Double(mover.start)
771	            + Double(mover.sourceIn) / speed
772	        return ReelTime.snapToFrame(Ticks(exact.rounded()), fps: fps)
773	    }
774	
775	    /// One mover's ops, each only when it changes something, ordered so
776	    /// that every span in between lies inside the old one or the final one
777	    /// (SY-10): a mover that grows moves first, one that shrinks or keeps
778	    /// its length changes speed first. A mover trimmed at its head (SY-16,
779	    /// `trimTo` the `trim_start` target S + e) changes speed first, so the
780	    /// trim advances its in point at the new speed, then trims, then moves.
781	    static func ops(
782	        clip: UInt32, delta: Ticks, from old: Double, to new: Double?, duration: Ticks,
783	        newDuration: Ticks, trimTo: Ticks? = nil
784	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
785	        let move: ReelOp? = delta != 0 ? ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [clip], delta: delta) : nil
786	        var speed: ReelOp?
787	        if let new = new, new != old {
788	            speed = ReelOp.setSpeed(clip: clip, rate: new, keepPitch: false)
789	        }
790	        if let trimTo {
791	            return [speed, ReelOp.trimStart(clip: clip, to: trimTo), move].compactMap { $0 }
792	        }
793	        if newDuration > duration {
794	            return [move, speed].compactMap { $0 }
795	        }
796	        return [speed, move].compactMap { $0 }
797	    }
798	}

801	/// Where Synchronize Audio's one GCC-PHAT refinement runs (#302; spec §11
802	/// SY-32, amending SY-20's and SY-29's centred region): moved out of
803	/// `AudioSync.swift`, where the region was the overlap's centre 30 s.
804	///
805	/// It is pure, as `plan` is: an overlap, the two readings' timeline-grid
806	/// features and masks and the line in, a range of anchor timeline samples
807	/// out. It only chooses WHERE: the refinement, its z and the gate are
808	/// `AudioSyncPHAT`'s and `plan`'s (SY-29), and there is still one region.
809	extension AudioSync {
810	
811	    /// SY-32's region: `overlap` (anchor timeline frames) ×128, in anchor
812	    /// timeline samples, when it holds at most W = `maximumRegionSamples /
813	    /// hop` frames; else the W frames whose features agree most along
814	    /// `line`. Frame f scores `Σ_k A[f, k]·M[m(f), k]`, A and M the features
815	    /// `standardised` as the match was (over the speech frames when it
816	    /// matched on speech), `m(f) = f − round((c + ρ·128f)/128)`, and 0 when
817	    /// f or m(f) lies outside its file. The start s in `[lo, hi − W]` with
818	    /// the greatest summed score wins; the centred start `⌊(lo + hi)/2⌋ −
819	    /// ⌊W/2⌋` is the first candidate, replaced only by a strictly greater
820	    /// sum or an equal one nearer it.
821	    static func refinementRegion(
822	        overlap: Range<Int>, anchorFrames: [Float], moverFrames: [Float], anchorSpeech: [Bool]?,
823	        moverSpeech: [Bool]?, matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn, line: AudioSyncPHAT.Line
824	    ) -> Range<Int> {
825	        let hop = SyncFeatures.hop
826	        let span = AudioSyncPHAT.maximumRegionSamples / hop
827	        let lo = overlap.lowerBound
828	        let hi = overlap.upperBound
829	        guard overlap.count > span else { return (lo * hop)..<(hi * hop) }
830	
831	        let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
832	        let onSpeech = matchedOn == .speech
833	        let a = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(anchorFrames, speech: onSpeech ? anchorSpeech : nil)
834	        let m = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(moverFrames, speech: onSpeech ? moverSpeech : nil)
835	        let anchorCount = a.count / width
836	        let moverCount = m.count / width
837	
838	        // prefix[i] = Σ score over the overlap's first i frames.
839	        var prefix = [Double](repeating: 0, count: overlap.count + 1)
840	        a.withUnsafeBufferPointer { anchor in
841	            m.withUnsafeBufferPointer { mover in
842	                for (index, f) in overlap.enumerated() {
843	                    let lag = ((line.intercept + line.rate * Double(f * hop)) / Double(hop))
844	                        .rounded()
845	                    let g = f - Int(lag)
846	                    var score = 0.0
847	                    if f >= 0, f < anchorCount, g >= 0, g < moverCount {
848	                        let x = f * width
849	                        let y = g * width
850	                        for k in 0..<width { score += Double(anchor[x + k]) * Double(mover[y + k]) }
851	                    }
852	                    prefix[index + 1] = prefix[index] + score
853	                }
854	            }
855	        }
856	        func sum(_ start: Int) -> Double { prefix[start - lo + span] - prefix[start - lo] }
857	
858	        let last = hi - span
859	        let centred = min(max(lo, (lo + hi) / 2 - span / 2), last)
860	        var best = centred
861	        var bestSum = sum(centred)
862	        for start in lo...last {
863	            let value = sum(start)
864	            if value > bestSum || (value == bestSum && abs(start - centred) < abs(best - centred)) {
865	                best = start
866	                bestSum = value
867	            }
868	        }
869	        return (best * hop)..<((best + span) * hop)
870	    }
871	}

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "The level meter"
description: Read the two-row meter in the timeline bar to see how loud the mix is while it plays, and whether it reaches full scale.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The level meter shows how high the mix you're hearing sits while the timeline plays, and warns you when a sample reaches full scale.

<AtAGlance where="The timeline bar, just left of the zoom controls" />

## What it shows

The meter shows what you hear: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, and the compressor and other effects. Press play and it moves. There's nothing to turn on.

It has two rows, one per channel, with the left channel on top. A mono track shows in both rows, and a track with more than two channels shows only its first two.

At normal speed it measures the mix itself, so two tracks playing the same sound read as one louder sound, and a sound and its inverse read as silence. At any other speed it adds up each track's level instead. That can read a little higher than the mix, and it can light the clip cell when the mix itself wouldn't reach full scale.

## Read the meter

Each row runs from −60 dB on the left to 0 dB on the right. The scale is even in dB, so the middle of a row is −30 dB. It has no tick marks.

| Part | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Solid bar** | The average (RMS) level. It rises at once and falls at 24 dB a second. |
| **Lighter wash** behind the bar | The instantaneous peak. It rises and falls the same way, and it's never shorter than the bar. |
| **Peak-hold mark** | The highest recent level. It stays for about 1.2 seconds, then falls at 12 dB a second. |
| **Clip cell** at the right end of each row | Lights for 2 seconds whenever a sample in that row reaches full scale. |

A level above 0 dB fills the row and goes no further, so the clip cell is what tells you the mix went over.

## When playback stops

The bars fall back to the floor. The peak-hold mark stops waiting and falls with them, and a lit clip cell stays lit for the rest of its 2 seconds. The whole meter is at rest within about 3 seconds.

## Good to know

- The meter shows peaks and average level, not loudness. For LUFS and true peak, use [the Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/).
- It shows the preview's mix. An export also goes through a master limiter, so what an export measures can differ. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
- There's one meter for the whole app. With two projects open, the meter in both windows follows the one that's playing, and stopping one project doesn't blank the meter while the other plays on.
- In a narrow window the meter gets smaller, and below 40 points wide it isn't drawn at all.
- The recorder panel has its own meter for the microphone. See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).

## Related

- [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/)
- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)

---
title: "The Loudness Meter"
description: Show a live column beside the preview that measures your mix in LUFS and true peak while it plays at normal speed.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Loudness Meter tells you how loud your mix really is, measured the way the loudness standards EBU R 128 and ITU-R BS.1770 measure it, while the preview plays at normal speed.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Loudness Meter"
  keys="⌃⌘L"
  where="A column at the right of the preview, left of the scopes"
/>

<Shot
  name="04c-editor-loudness.preview"
  alt="The preview with the Loudness column at its right edge, before anything has played. The column has a Reset arrow at the top, M and S bars on a scale from 0 to −48 with a thin blue line across them just above −18, then Momentary, Short-term, Integrated and True peak max, each reading a dash, and a note saying this is the mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
/>

## Show the meter

Choose **View ▸ Loudness Meter** or press <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd>. The same command hides it, and the menu item has a tick while the column is showing. The column is 132 points wide and as tall as the preview pane, and the picture makes room for it.

Then play the timeline at normal speed. The figures start at "—" and fill in as Frame Job measures.

## What it measures

The meter measures the mix you hear, including every clip's and track's sound, and it follows each track's own position, so a gap between clips doesn't disturb it. It only reads what plays. It never changes the project or an export.

Measuring carries on while the column is hidden. If you show it partway through a pass, the figures already include what has played.

A mono track counts in both channels. A track with more than two channels counts by its first two.

## The four figures

| Figure | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| **Momentary** | The last 0.4 seconds. |
| **Short-term** | The last 3 seconds. |
| **Integrated** | Everything measured since the last reset, with quiet passages left out as the standard says. |
| **True peak max** | The highest true peak since the last reset. It turns coral above −1 dBTP. |

Figures have one decimal place, such as `−18.4 LUFS` or `−0.6 dBTP`.

| You see | It means |
| --- | --- |
| "—" | There's no figure yet. Momentary needs 0.4 seconds of measuring and Short-term needs 3. Integrated stays at "—" until something loud enough to count has played, so it stays there through digital silence. |
| "−∞" | Digital silence. |

## The M and S bars

The two bars show Momentary (**M**) and Short-term (**S**) on a scale from −48 to 0 LUFS, with a tick every 6 LU. A bar is empty while its figure is "—", and during digital silence.

## The target line

A thin line in the accent colour crosses both bars at the target in the [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) row, which is −16 LUFS unless you've changed it. It shows you where the mix sits against the level Normalize aims for.

The line moves as soon as you change the target, even while the preview is paused. The target can go as low as −50 LUFS, and anything below −48 draws at the bottom of the scale. The line stays at the stored target when Normalize is in Peak mode.

## Start measuring again

Click the **Reset** button, the ↺ at the top of the column. All four figures go back to "—" and the next sound starts a new measurement.

The meter also starts again by itself when you jump somewhere else, such as a seek, the loop going round, or playing from another place. It does the same if Frame Job can't keep up with the audio, because a measurement with a hole in it would be wrong.

These don't restart it:

- Pausing and playing on. Nothing is counted twice.
- An edit.
- A gap between clips.
- Holding a menu open.
- Stepping back by less than a second.

When playback stops, the figures stay where they were.

## Measuring only at normal speed

The meter measures at ×1 only. At any other speed, such as while you [shuttle](/timeline/playback/):

- Momentary and Short-term show "—" and their bars go empty.
- The note reads "Measured only at normal speed."
- Integrated and True peak max keep their values.

When you stop, Momentary and Short-term go back to their last normal-speed values.

## The note under the figures

The note says what's being measured, and when to take the figures with care.

| The note says | When |
| --- | --- |
| "The mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness and master limiter." | Usually. |
| "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter." | While any track has a [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/). They're approximate in the preview and exact in an export. |
| "Measured only at normal speed." | While playing at any other speed. |

An export with a loudness target changes the level after this point, and the master limiter holds its peaks under the ceiling, so the export's own report can differ from what you see here. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

## Good to know

- The meter belongs to its window. A new window starts with the column off and the meter empty.
- Nothing is saved. Closing the window ends the measurement, and the column is off the next time you open the project.

## With an agent

No agent tool shows this meter or reads it. An agent reads loudness from an export's report instead. See [Tools: export](/mcp/tools-export/).

## Related

- [The level meter](/audio/level-meter/)
- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)

---
title: "Synchronize Audio"
description: Line up a camera and a separate recorder, or any clips of the same moment, by matching their sound.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Synchronize Audio lines up two or more clips by their sound. The usual case is a camera clip and a separate audio recorder that captured the same moment. It finds where the sound matches, moves the clips into place and corrects any clock drift, all as one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio"
  tools="sync_audio"
  needs="Nothing. The matching and the voice detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Line up clips

<Steps>

1. Put each clip on its own track. They don't need to be close to each other.

2. If the recorder holds several similar stretches, trim it roughly around the camera's sound, so it [matches the right one](#matching-by-sound).

3. Select the clips.

4. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

5. Wait for the [Synchronizing Audio sheet](#the-synchronizing-audio-sheet) to finish.

</Steps>

One clip, the [anchor](#the-anchor), stays where it is. Every other clip slides along its own track until its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. The whole command is one undo step, named **Synchronize Audio**.

If Frame Job is sure of the match, it's applied straight away. If it isn't, Frame Job [asks you first](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).

It's all or nothing. If any clip can't be matched, nothing moves, and [the reasons are listed](#when-it-wont-run).

## Which clips it takes

**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** is available when at least two selected clips can play sound and aren't [nests](/editing/nests/).

Anything else in the selection is left out without a message: a nest, a still, a title, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off. To line up clips inside a nest, open it with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and select them there.

## The anchor

Frame Job picks the anchor this way:

1. Among the selected clips that have a picture, the one that starts earliest. If none has a picture, all of them are considered.
2. If two start at the same time, the one on the rearmost track.
3. If they're still tied, the one created first.

So a camera clip stays put and the recorder moves to it. The anchor is never moved or trimmed, and its speed doesn't change.

## Matching by sound

Each file's sound is analysed once, after it's imported, into a form that isn't thrown off by differences in gain, microphone or room. Frame Job compares the files, not the clips, so a clip's volume and effects make no difference.

- **Speech comes first.** When both clips hold at least 2 seconds of speech, as judged by the on-device voice model, only the speech is compared. Otherwise all the sound is.
- **The trimmed parts come first.** Frame Job looks within the parts each clip is trimmed to, when both are at least 2 seconds long. It searches the whole files only if that finds no usable match and at least one clip is trimmed.

:::tip
A recording with two similar stretches can match the wrong one. Trimming the recorder roughly around the camera's sound tells Frame Job which one you mean.
:::

## The waveform check

Sounding alike isn't enough, because two takes of the same words can look like a match. So a match is used only if the two waveforms also line up there, as a clear peak within 48 ms. Frame Job checks up to 30 seconds of the overlap, where the sound agrees most, in the speech band of 300 to 3,400 Hz.

The same check fine-tunes the offset to less than a frame.

## Moves land on whole frames

Clips move by a whole number of frames at the project's frame rate, so up to half a frame of constant offset can remain. At 30 fps that's about 17 ms.

## The head trim

If a clip would have to start before 0:00 to line up, it loses that much from its start instead, and starts at 0:00 in sync. Frame Job trims only what it has to. It won't do this if less than a frame of the clip would be left.

## Drift correction

Two devices' clocks never run at quite the same rate, so a recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift along the overlap and corrects it by playing the moved clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1.

The correction is part of the same undo step. There's no drift figure to read. What changes is the clip's speed, which shows in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/), for example ×1.0004, with **Keep pitch** turned off. The clip gets very slightly longer or shorter to match.

Drift is left alone when:

- it's under 5 ms across the overlap
- it's too small to tell from no drift, meaning under three times its own uncertainty
- correcting it would take more than 0.2 % from ×1
- too little of the overlap matches to measure it

:::note
The correction is a plain resample, so the pitch moves very slightly with the speed. Like any clip with Keep pitch off at a speed other than ×1, the clip's sound is [rendered in the background](/speed/keep-pitch/#tape-pitch-is-rendered-in-the-background). It's briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change. An export waits for it.
:::

## The Synchronizing Audio sheet

Matching runs in the background behind a **Synchronizing Audio** sheet, with a progress bar and the line "Matching the sound of N clips…". Nothing moves until a match is found.

**Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the sheet and leaves everything as it was.

If the project changes while the matching runs, for example because an agent edits it, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.

## When it won't run

Frame Job beeps and lists every reason in [the strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip), naming each clip by its number. The strip shows three lines, so hover over it to read a long one.

It checks each clip first, and won't start matching until they all pass. A clip can't be lined up when it:

- plays no sound in the timeline
- is still being analysed. Its sound or speech analysis hasn't finished, so try again in a moment.
- comes from a file with under 2 seconds of sound
- plays more than 0.2 % away from ×1. Set it back to ×1 first.
- plays at a rate other than its speed setting
- plays [reversed](/speed/reverse/)
- [ramps its speed](/speed/speed-ramps/), because a speed action changes its rate over its length

The rest come up during the matching:

- Two of the clips are on one track. Each needs its own.
- A clip has no sound to line up by, because its analysis found no sound at all.
- Nothing matches. See [When nothing matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/#when-nothing-matches).
- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the waveforms don't line up there, for example two takes of the same words. They aren't one recording.
- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the two share under 2 seconds of waveform there, too little to confirm it's one recording.
- A clip would lose so much of its head that less than a frame is left.
- A clip would never play at the same time as the anchor once lined up. Extend its trim, or the anchor's.
- A clip would overlap another clip on its own track after the move. Move that clip out of the way, or put this one on a free track.

## Good to know

If the clips are already in sync, nothing changes and Frame Job beeps. Choosing the command a second time on the same clips does this.

## With an agent

`sync_audio` does the same thing, with two differences. An agent can name the anchor, and it's told by name when it passes a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the menu leaves those out. It also reports each clip's offset, confidence and drift, which the menu doesn't show. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).

## Related

- [Confident and weak matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/)
- [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/)
- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
- [Nests](/editing/nests/)

---
title: "Confident and weak matches"
description: How Synchronize Audio grades a match, what the Weak match sheet asks you, and what to do when nothing matches.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

[Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) grades every match it finds. A confident match is applied straight away, a weak one is asked about first, and anything less moves nothing.

<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio" tools="sync_audio" />

Each possible offset gets a **confidence**: a score for how far it stands out from every other offset Frame Job tried. A high score means one offset is clearly right. Frame Job keeps up to four candidates, each about a second or more from the others.

Either grade must also pass [the waveform check](/audio/synchronize-audio/#the-waveform-check). A match that fails it isn't used, however high its confidence.

## Confident matches

A match is confident when its best candidate has a confidence of at least 10, and is at least 1.5 above the next candidate. A confident match is applied straight away.

## The Weak match sheet

A match is weak when no candidate is confident, but the best one within about 3 seconds of where the clip already sits has a confidence of at least 4. A weak match might be unrelated sound, so it's never applied without asking. A **Weak match** sheet appears:

> Weak match: move “record.aifc” 0.80 s earlier (trimming 0.80 s off its head)?

A clip that doesn't need to move, only to have its drift corrected, is asked about this way:

> Weak match: play “record.aifc” at ×1.0004, correcting its drift?

When several clips are weak, one sheet lists them all, separated by semicolons.

Under the question, the sheet gives the anchor's name, each match's confidence and the rule it fell short of.

| Choose | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Apply** (the default) | Makes all the changes as one undo step, including those for any clips that matched confidently. |
| **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Leaves everything as it is, including clips that matched confidently. |

If the project changed while the sheet was up, **Apply** moves nothing. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.

A weak match that wouldn't change anything isn't asked about.

## When nothing matches

If no candidate is confident or weak, nothing moves. [The strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip) names the offsets Frame Job did find and their confidences, for example:

> no matching sound found between clip 1 and clip 2: in the played windows, moving clip 2 by +0.77 s (confidence 4.31) or −12.40 s (3.90)

"The played windows" are the parts each clip is trimmed to, and "the whole files" are listed too when those were searched. A plus sign means later and a minus sign means earlier. Hover over the strip to read the whole message.

To try again:

<Steps>

1. Pick the offset that looks right. You might know roughly where the clip belongs, or one figure may be well ahead of the others.

2. Move the clip by about that much, so it sits within 3 seconds of the match.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** again. A candidate near the clip with a confidence of at least 4 now comes up as a weak match.

</Steps>

If the message ends "too little room to compare their sound", Frame Job found no candidates at all. Check that both clips have enough sound to compare, and try longer trims.

## Good to know

The whole files are searched only when the trimmed parts give neither a confident nor a weak match. A weak match in the trimmed parts ends the search, so if you cancel it, widen or narrow the trims before trying again.

## With an agent

An agent gets no sheet. A weak match moves nothing and the agent is told the move it would make, so it should ask you. It applies the match only once you've agreed. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/).

## Related

- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)

Each feature's page lists what can stop it, and [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/) gathers them in one place.

A typed Start, Length or end value on an action shows the strip too. Dragging an action's band never does. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

## A drop that springs back

3:Frame Job mixes sound from every clip that has it: a camera clip, an audio-only file, a microphone recording or a nest. Each clip has its own level, fades, ducking, voice isolation, a voice effect, channel choice, EQ, hum removal, noise reduction, gate, leveller, de-esser, compressor, pan and mono fold, and a true-peak limiter, and each track can be muted or soloed and has its own volume, pan, compressor and limiter. Four commands do the measuring for you. Normalize sets a clip's level from its loudness (or its loudest moment), Enhance Voice sets a voice recording up for speech from its own measurements, Match Audio gives clips another clip's loudness and tone, and Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by their sound. The preview and the export use the same mix, so what you hear while editing is what gets written, except that every export also holds its peaks under −1 dBTP with a master limiter the preview doesn't have, and a track's compressor and limiter are exact in an export but approximate in the preview (see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter)).
137:*Agents:* `enhance_voice` (`clips`; optional `target_lufs` from −50 to −5, default −16). Each row of `enhanced` gives the measurements (`measured_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `speech_seconds`, `floor_lufs`, `floor_gap_db`, `pause_peak_dbfs`, `sibilance_share`, `speech_range_lu`: null with under 3 s of speech), `set` (exactly the `set_audio` keys written), `reasons` (one sentence per rule), `volume`, `processed_lufs`, `renders`, `result_lufs` and `result_true_peak_dbtp` as the last render measured them, and `limited_by`. Skips are under `skipped`. A second call answers "Enhance Voice made no change".
154:*Agents:* `match_audio` (`reference`, `clips`; optional `loudness` and `eq`, both default true, refused when both are false). The answer gives `reference` (`clip`, `media`, `lufs`, `speech_seconds`), `target_lufs` (null with loudness off), and a row per clip under `matched`: `set` (exactly the `set_audio` keys written), `eq` and `eq_fit_rms_db` (how far the fitted EQ is from the measured difference), `volume`, `measured_lufs`, `processed_lufs`, `result_lufs`, `result_true_peak_dbtp`, `limited_by` and `renders`. Skips are under `skipped`. A second call answers "Match Audio made no change".
207:With **Clip Length**, ducking follows the clip's length on the timeline, not whether anyone is talking. The other audio stays lowered for the whole length of the ducking clip, through pauses, and comes back up only after the clip ends. You can therefore see exactly when ducking applies by looking at the timeline. If the attack is longer than the clip, the level never fully reaches Level, and the release starts from wherever it got to.
571:- **Approximate in the preview.** The preview plays a track's sound in more than one piece where its clips overlap (a crossfade, or a nest's tracks), and it runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately, so the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while editing. Measured on two clips at −1 dBFS crossfading under a limiter at −6 dBTP, the preview's true peak was 5.2 dB over the ceiling; the export held it. The Loudness Meter says "approximate" while any track has a compressor or limiter.
572:- **What hears them.** The preview, the level meter and the Loudness Meter (approximately), and every export. Normalize, the Loudness read-out, Enhance Voice and Match Audio work on the clip itself, before the track, and don't.
616:The figures are the mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness setting and its master limiter, and the column says so. While any track has a compressor or limiter, it says they are approximate (see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter)). An export with a loudness target changes the level after this point, and the master limiter holds its peaks under the ceiling, so its report can differ. The column is per window and turns off when you close the window.
709:- A track's compressor and limiter are approximate in the preview wherever its clips overlap (a crossfade, a nest's tracks); see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter). A nest's own tracks have none, and scrubbing doesn't hear them.
720:- Attach Audio needs the picture and its sound to cover exactly the same time. Undo a J-cut or L-cut, or trim the two to match, before attaching.
